### 1. About processing of personal data

Personal data is all information that can be directly or indirectly linked to a living, physical person. Examples of personal data are: name, e-mail address, telephone number and IP address. Processing of personal data is any automated use of personal data - such as collecting, creating, analyzing, sharing, and deleting personal data.

There are laws and regulations on how companies may process personal data, so-called data protection laws. Different data protection laws apply to different types of use of personal data, and in different parts of the world. An example of a data protection law that is relevant for our use of your personal data, as described in this privacy policy, is the EU Data Protection Regulation (2016/679, "GDPR").

Most obligations under the GDPR apply to the so-called data controller. A data controller is the entity that decides for which purposes personal data will be processed, and how the processing will be executed. The data controller can use a so-called data processor. A data processor is an entity that is only allowed to process personal data as instructed by the data controller, and may not use the personal data for its own purposes.

We are the data controller when we process your personal data as described in this Privacy policy.

# Regional Account Relationship Manager – IFA Distribution (Scotland & Northern Ireland)

OverviewApplication

**What is Flagstone?**

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

**A feel for our culture**

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we *can* change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.  
  
But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

**Does this sound like you?**

Flagstone is the UK's leading cash platform with £19bn in AuA and a mandate to reach £50bn by 2028. The IFA and wealth manager channel is one of the most significant growth opportunities in front of the business with over 1,400 registered IFA firms on the platform, strong existing relationships to deepen, and a large addressable market of independent advisers who have yet to engage with us at all.

The ARM role combines proactive business development with ongoing relationship management. You will be identifying and engaging IFA firms in Scotland and Northern Ireland, introducing the Flagstone proposition, training advisers on how to use the platform, and building the trusted, consistent relationships that turn a registered firm into an active referral partner.

**What You'll Be Doing**

**Proactive Partner Engagement & Development**

* Own your territory of IFA firms and wealth managers, taking personal responsibility for the breadth and depth of engagement and the referral activity it generates
* Spend the substantial majority of your time in the field visiting adviser firms, attending regional industry events, and building face-to-face relationships that create consistent, long-term referral partners
* Proactively identify and approach IFA firms not yet working with Flagstone, introducing the proposition and beginning the relationship development process from first meeting to active referral
* Work to deepen engagement with registered firms that are not yet actively referring, understanding what is holding them back and taking targeted action to unlock their activity
* Grow the volume and value of referrals from existing active partners by helping them identify more clients who could benefit from Flagstone

**Proposition Training & Education**

* Deliver clear, confident, and compelling presentations of the Flagstone proposition to IFA firms individually and in group settings
* Train advisers on the Flagstone referral portal and onboarding process, reducing friction and building confidence so that making a referral feels straightforward
* Keep partner firms up to date with product developments and platform enhancements
* Use insight from adviser conversations to feed back proposition gaps, platform friction points, or competitive pressures

**Reactive Support & Partner Feedback**

* Act as a knowledgeable and responsive point of contact for your partner firms when they have questions about Flagstone, the referral process, or platform features
* Resolve queries with pace and accuracy, always closing the loop with the adviser
* Act as a structured source of intelligence from the IFA market back into Flagstone, capturing and communicating what advisers are telling you about the platform, proposition, and competitive landscape
* Feed adviser feedback directly into the product development process, flagging friction points, missing features, and enhancements that would most meaningfully increase referral activity

**Pipeline & Performance**

* Maintain a clear and current picture of your regional pipeline through tracking firm engagement levels, referral volumes, and conversion activity
* Report regularly to the Relationships Team Lead on the health of your territory - what is working, where the opportunities are, and where support is needed

**What You'll Bring**

**Field Sales & Relationship Management**

* Experience in a field based sales or relationship management role, with a proven track record of building trusted commercial relationships face to face
* Genuine comfort being out in the field every day, covering a broad and geographically diverse territory - you need to be energised by travel, variety, and independence
* The personal presence and communication skills to represent Flagstone confidently in front of independent financial advisers, wealth managers, and compliance officers

**Financial Services Knowledge**

* A solid understanding of the IFA and wealth manager market - how independent advice firms are structured, how advisers make recommendations, and how cash management fits within a client's financial plan
* Familiarity with the regulatory landscape: directly authorised firms, Appointed Representatives, and network members
* Sufficient financial literacy to have credible conversations about cash, interest rates, FSCS protection, and multi-bank diversification

**Commercial Drive & Self-Direction**

* A commercially motivated self-starter who takes personal ownership of regional performance and manages their own diary and territory plan
* Organised and disciplined in how you manage a complex regional portfolio: you plan your visits, track your pipeline, and follow up consistently across a large number of relationships simultaneously

**How we reward you:**

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

* Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance
* Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.
* A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.
* Around the World scheme - 3 months work from anywhere scheme
* Mental wellbeing support - Access therapy and mental health sessions through Spill
* Learning and development - £1,000 personal development budget to help you grow in your role.
* Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded
* Medical cash plan - To help you with the costs of dental and optical expenses
* Life insurance and Income Protection- four times your annual salary for peace of mind
* Matched pension contributions up to 5%
* 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days
* Enhanced Parental Leave - enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.

**All are welcome.**

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

At Flatpay, we're building products that make running a business simpler.
Flatpay is one of Europe's fastest-growing fintechs. Founded in Copenhagen in 2022, we've grown to 100,000+ merchants across seven markets - Denmark, Finland, France, Italy, the UK, Germany, and the Netherlands - and recently became Denmark's fastest-ever unicorn at a €1.5B valuation.
Thousands of merchants rely on our payment solutions every day. As we continue expanding our POS offering, we're looking for a Senior Product Manager who can turn complex merchant needs into products that are intuitive, reliable, and commercially impactful.
We're now scaling aggressively across Europe and investing heavily in product. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage a backlog from a distance. We need a product leader who enjoys spending time with customers, challenging assumptions, making difficult prioritization decisions, and working closely with engineers, designers, commercial teams, and leadership to shape the future of our POS platform.
What you'll be responsible for
You'll own a meaningful slice of our POS product - the software that runs the front of house for thousands of restaurants, cafés, retail stores, and salons across Europe - and be accountable for delivering outcomes, not just features.
Our merchants are not procurement teams at large enterprises. They're owner-operators. That means the bar for usability, reliability, and clarity is brutally high — a confusing settings menu or a slow checkout flow costs them real sales on a Friday night. You'll spend real time in those venues, not just in Figma.
Your work will include:
Defining and driving product strategy for POS solutions across multiple merchant segments
Sit with merchants and watch them work. Learn the difference between what they say in interviews and what they actually do on a busy Friday lunch. Bring those insights back into the roadmap
Translating customer insights, business objectives, and technical constraints into clear product direction
Understand the critical merchant value and plan the MVP rather than big deliveries
Working closely with engineering and design teams to deliver high-quality solutions at pace
Using data, customer feedback, and market insights to evaluate product performance and guide decisions
Helping establish product management best practices as Flatpay continues to scale
What we're looking for
We're less interested in whether you've worked with a specific framework and more interested in how you think and operate. We hope you are comfortable operating in a hyper-growth environment where the org chart and the roadmap both move fast.
You likely bring:
6+ years of product management experience in software, fintech, payments, POS, SaaS, or a similarly complex domain
Background launching products 0->1 and 1->10 into multiple European markets
The ability to navigate ambiguity and create clarity for teams around you
Experience working with cross-functional product development teams
Confidence communicating with both technical and non-technical audiences
A data-informed mindset without becoming data-dependent
Excellent written and spoken English. Danish, French, Italian or German is a plus, not a requirement
Strong commercial instinct. You think about adoption, revenue, and unit economics, not just feature usage
Willingness to spend time in the field with merchants across our markets
AI literacy and implementation into everyday life and products is highly required
Bonus points if you have experience with:
Payments or acquiring
Point-of-sale systems
Merchant-facing products
Omnichannel commerce
Subscription or transaction-based business models
Familiarity with Android-based payment hardware (PAX, Ingenico, or similar)
After your 3 months, you have:
Built deep knowledge of merchant needs and operational realities across multiple markets
Established a clear product direction in a collaboration with other PMs and Product Director
Built deep knowledge of Flatpay product offering and identify gaps
Delivered meaningful improvements that merchants actively value
Created strong partnerships across product, engineering, design, commercial teams, and leadership
Contributed to a stronger product culture across Flatpay
Why Flatpay?
We're building in a market where reliability matters, customer expectations evolve quickly, and product decisions have a direct impact on real businesses.
You'll join a company with ambitious growth plans, short decision-making paths, and the opportunity to influence products used every day by merchants across Europe.
If you're excited by solving real-world problems, working closely with customers, and building products that combine software, payments, and commerce, we'd love to hear from you.

# principal investigator, biological computing

**frontier** · Cambridge, UK · full-time, permanent
founding scientific leadership role (CTO/CSO equivalent)
salary: £100,000 to £180,000 (approx. US$136,000 to US$246,000), plus 1 to 4% equity

## about frontier computing

*frontier computing* works on cultured neural tissue as a computational substrate.

The underlying observation is not new. Biological neurones in vivo perform inference at very low power, several orders of magnitude below what a comparable silicon system would draw, and the cells manufacture themselves.

What has been missing is any serious attempt to find out whether that can be turned into something reproducible, scalable and cheap enough to be useful. For most of the past decade the answer was clearly no, for well understood technical reasons. Several of those reasons have weakened: iPSC differentiation protocols have become more reliable, microfluidic culture systems now survive well past the four week mark, and optimising reading from, and writing into, cultured tissue with multi-electrode arrays is now better understood than ever previously.

We should be plain about where we are. **We have learning on the first scalable substrate, and a strongly supported hypothesis that further buildout of substrate size will bring further computational results, enabling energy efficient computation at scale while circumventing von Neumann architecture bottlenecks.**

That is a starting point, but the significant work ahead is to establish whether the mechanisms we are seeing are reproducible, generalise to more structured circuits, and survive being scaled. Scaling credit assignment is an incredible challenge and an open question within biological neural networks, and one that our company is actively solving.

-

## the research programme

Three codependent problems define the work.

### 1. the cost of culturing substrates at scale

Large scale neuronal culture is currently expensive enough that very few groups can do sustained work with it. We think that is the binding constraint on the whole field, and that it is more tractable than it looks.

The useful denominator is cost per neurone-hour rather than cost per millilitre of media, which decomposes multiplicatively into chemistry, volume and density. Within chemistry the drivers are not where one might expect: in a representative maintenance medium the basal medium and the B-27 supplement together account for the large majority of per-millilitre cost, while the recombinant factors, which are by far the most expensive per milligram, contribute very little because they are dosed at trivial mass. Both of the dominant inputs are commodities, and commodities respond to process work rather than to chemistry.

Volume and density compound on top of chemistry, and have received less attention, largely because the protocols in general use were developed for developmental biology rather than for sustained culture. There is meaningful headroom across the product of the three.

We have made real progress here, and it is the most mature of the three programmes. The goal is not a proprietary advantage in reagent purchasing. It is to bring large scale neuronal culture within reach of ordinary experimental budgets, including our own.

### 2. reproducing core neuronal training mechanisms

Most work in this area imports the reinforcement learning apparatus from silicon: define a global reward, propagate it back, and hope the tissue converges. This is expensive to build and expensive to run, and it scales poorly as neurone count rises and credit assignment gets harder.

We are interested in the opposite approach, which is to let the biology do as much of the learning as it already knows how to do. Local mechanisms, spike-timing dependent plasticity and neuromodulator-gated plasticity among them, are implemented natively by the tissue at no cost to us. If a training environment can be designed so that the desired change is what those mechanisms produce anyway, the control apparatus becomes much simpler and the approach scales with neurone count rather than with the complexity of the reward circuitry.

Our current work is in **cortical computation**, and the near-term direction is to extend it toward **hippocampal circuit work**, where the relationship between architecture, plasticity and function is better characterised and where there is a substantial literature to argue with. The immediate scientific question is whether the learning we see on a simple substrate reproduces in a structured one.

### 3. building out mature neuronal cultures at scale

Culture size is limited by oxygen and nutrient diffusion, and beyond a few millimetres the core of a construct necroses. This is a well known constraint and it is the proximate reason nobody has built a biological system with the connected mass that would make any of this interesting.

Maturation is the second half of the problem and is often treated separately, which we think is a mistake. A large culture of immature neurones is not useful; the target is tissue that is both sizeable and functionally mature, held in that state for the duration of a workload rather than for the duration of an experiment.

Vascularisation is an approach much of the literature takes, and progress there is real. We are already performing our own tissue scaling, and because of this our roadmap is now more closely focused toward culturing more physiologically mature tissue with greater respective computational capacities. We want to hire talent that understands the problem space has moved, and that we are now not only dealing with scale, but also codesigning phenotypic expression with our tissue construct approach to produce *mature* tissue at scale.

-

## about the role

This is the founding scientific leadership position at frontier. We have called it Principal Investigator in this job posting rather than Chief Scientific Officer because the substance of the job is closer to running a research group than to running a corporate function: you would set the scientific agenda, choose the problems, build the team, and be accountable for whether the science works. The title officially will be CSO, but your functional work will have much more freedom than this role traditionally implies, given the greenfield nature of the field.

However, your work will fundamentally be application-oriented, designed to push the capacity for biological substrate approaches. This is not a role performing blue-skies research, and the programme will have to be justified towards our business goals. First and foremost, we are looking for someone who understands these tradeoffs, and appreciates that the science they are pursuing must benefit our commercialisation strategy: building larger tissues with both greater and denser computational and memory capacities.

You would be the first senior scientific hire, and as part of that role you will define the future composition of the team alongside the CEO, and help build out a scientific programme that drives substrate progress and feeds into our commercialisation efforts.

### what you would be doing

**Research leadership.** Own the scientific agenda across the three programmes above. Decide what is attacked, in what order, with what resources, and decide what is stopped. Design the experimental programme that takes us from the substrate we have now to something considerably larger, with the network kept in the loop rather than distilled away.

**Building the group.** Recruit and lead the founding scientific team across wet lab, instrumentation and the computational side of the training work. You would have real latitude over who joins and how the group is organised. If you hold views about how research groups ought to be run, this is an unusual opportunity to act on them.

**Go City is transforming the way people see and experience the world’s greatest destinations.**We give our customers total flexibility to choose the experiences, tours and activities they want to visit at incredible savings.

The Director of CRM owns the relationship between Go City and the people who buy from us - before, between and after every purchase. This is the most strategically important growth lever we have that isn’t paid media: as customer acquisition costs rise across our OTA-driven channels, the value we extract from each customer we already have is what protects our margin and our long-term growth.  
  
We are explicit about what this role is and isn’t. It is not running a transactional email calendar, sending the same discount to everyone and reporting on open rates. It is building genuine customer relationships across the lifecycle - understanding who our customers are, what they’re worth, what makes them come back, and designing the programmes that move them up the value curve. The difference between a CRM that sends transactional messages and a CRM that builds relationships and lifetime value is the difference between this role done badly and done well, and it's the single most important thing we are hiring for.  
  
You will sit alongside the Director of Paid and the Head of SEO as a peer in the marketing leadership team, owning the retention and value side of the growth equation while they own acquisition. You will be expected to hold your own in strategic debate with them, with finance and with the executive team - not just to execute a plan handed to you.

## What you'll own

**Lifecycle & Retention Strategy**

* Own the end-to-end customer lifecycle strategy - acquisition handover, onboarding, activation, repeat purchase, win-back and lapsed reactivation - across gocity.com and our city pass brands.
* Treat the customer journey as one product rather than a series of disconnected campaigns; design the nurture, trigger and lifecycle flows that move customers between stages.
* Move the organisation away from a discount-led, signup-volume mindset toward a value-led model, and build the evidence and the case to do so.

**Customer Value & Commercial Ownership**

* Own customer lifetime value as a metric you understand, can decompose and can move - including the LTV difference between discount-acquired and full-price customers, and what that means for how we market.
* Define success for the CRM channel in outcome terms (retention, repeat rate, margin, LTV) rather than activity or input metrics (sends, signups, open rates).
* Build the commercial case for CRM investment and defend it with data in front of finance and the executive team.
* Develop a segmentation and value framework so the right customers receive the right contact, rather than everyone receiving the same offer.

**Programme & Loyalty**

* Design and run the loyalty and retention programmes that reduce our dependency on paid acquisition over time.
* Own the email, push and lifecycle channels operationally - deliverability, data capture, consent and the underlying CRM platform - while keeping the focus on relationship and value, not volume.
* Partner with the data and analytics team to build the measurement that tells us whether the channel is genuinely creating value, including clean before/after reads and defined kill criteria for tests.

**Leadership & Influence**

* Lead, hire and develop the CRM / lifecycle team, raising the strategic bar of the function.
* Operate as a true peer to the Director of Paid and Head of SEO — contributing a strong, structured point of view to marketing strategy rather than waiting to be directed.
* Bring forward strategic proposals, stress-test the proposals of others constructively, and think in trade-offs rather than absolutes.

**Success at 6 months**

* A clear, evidenced CRM strategy that the leadership team has bought into, framed in customer value rather than signup volume.
* A working segmentation and value framework, with the highest-value cohorts identified and treated differently.
* At least one well-designed lifecycle or retention programme live and measured properly, with a clean read on its commercial impact.
* A credible point of view on the discount-led vs value-led question, backed by LTV evidence, ready to inform wider marketing strategy.
* A CRM function visibly operating as a strategic peer to acquisition, not a downstream execution channel.

## What you'll bring

* Significant experience leading CRM, lifecycle or retention at a senior level in a consumer / ecommerce business, with demonstrable ownership of customer value and retention outcomes (not just campaign delivery).
* A track record of building genuine lifecycle programmes - segmentation, value-based contact strategy, loyalty or retention - that moved a commercial metric.
* Strong commercial and numerical literacy: comfortable with LTV, cohort and margin analysis, and able to translate them into strategy.
* Experience owning a CRM / lifecycle platform and the data, consent and deliverability that underpin it.
* Experience leading and developing a team, and operating as a peer to other marketing leaders.

**Bonus, not essential**

* Experience in travel, attractions, ticketing or another considered-purchase consumer category.
* Experience shifting an organisation away from a discount-led model toward a value-led one, including managing the short-term trade-offs that involves.
* Familiarity with experimentation discipline - clean test design, before/after reads, pre-agreed kill criteria.

**This job is for you if**

* You have a clear strategic view and can articulate a position — not a series of “it depends” caveats - and you can defend it under challenge.
* You think in customer value and trade-offs, not channel activity, and instinctively reach for data rather than assertion when you don’t know an answer.
* You understand that a transactional relationship is not CRM, and can explain what real relationship building and value creation look like in our category.
* You can answer questions like: how would you measure the CRM channel if signup volume wasn’t a metric? What’s the LTV gap between a discounted and a full-price customer, and how would you find out if you didn’t know?
* You have a forward view: you can say where the channel should be in 12–18 months and what structural risks we’d be foolish to ignore.
* You’re genuinely “can-do”: you turn a strategic position into a concrete plan and get it moving, rather than only critiquing.

**This may not be a good fit if you**

* You’d rather run a transactional email calendar - sending the same discount to everyone and reporting on open rates - than build genuine customer relationships and lifetime value.
* You prefer a series of “it depends” caveats to holding a clear, defensible position under challenge.
* You’d rather execute a plan handed to you than hold your own in strategic debate with peers, finance and the executive team.

# Senior Fundraising Executive - Community & DIY Fundraising

Do you love working with people and building meaningful relationships? Are you an excellent communicator who thrives in a busy and varied role and takes pride in delivering exceptional supporter stewardship? If so, we'd love to hear from you.

We're looking for an organised and proactive individual to build and manage relationships with a portfolio of mid and high-value community supporters, primarily DIY (in aid of) fundraisers who organise their own fundraising events and activities, alongside other community fundraising audiences including Clubs & Groups, In Memory supporters and some patient families, including bereaved families. You'll inspire supporters to maximise their fundraising while ensuring they feel valued, recognised and supported throughout their journey.

No two days are the same. You'll work closely with other Senior Executives in the Community Fundraising team, colleagues from across the charity and the Senior Manager to deliver exceptional stewardship, develop new supporter experiences and collaborate on projects that help some of our most committed fundraisers have the biggest possible impact for Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity.  
    
This position is a 12 month fixed term contract role until September 2027

**Salary**

The salary for this position is £38,371 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office.

In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate.

## Key Responsibilities

* Manage a portfolio of mid and high-value community supporters, primarily DIY fundraisers, alongside other community fundraising audiences including Clubs & Groups, In Memory supporters and some patient families, including bereaved families, building trusted relationships that maximise fundraising and encourage long-term support.
* Deliver personalised stewardship through regular contact, fundraising advice, recognition opportunities and tailored supporter experiences, ensuring every supporter feels valued and supported.
* Identify opportunities to re-engage existing supporters and welcome new high-potential fundraisers into your portfolio.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues across fundraising and supporter services to deliver exceptional supporter experiences and identify opportunities for supporters to deepen their involvement with GOSH Charity.
* Support the development and delivery of new stewardship initiatives that help grow community fundraising and enhance the supporter journey.
* Maintain accurate supporter records and contribute to income forecasting and reporting.

## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

* Highly organised with the ability to manage multiple relationships and priorities simultaneously.
* Confident communicator who can tailor their approach to different supporters and identify opportunities to maximise fundraising and engagement.
* Experience using CRM systems and is comfortable maintaining accurate records and using data to inform relationship management.

# Senior Software Engineer

Are you a hands-on Software Engineer who wants to build great technology, solve interesting problems and help shape how an organisation engineers for the future?

Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Digital Experience Engineering team and play a key role in Driven by Data**,** our digital and data transformation programme.

You'll initially have a major focus on Seamless Data—modernising how data moves between our systems and partners by replacing fragmented, manual integrations with secure, reliable and scalable services.

But the opportunity is broader than one programme. As a permanent member of our Engineering team, you'll work across software, integrations, cloud technology and digital experiences—taking technical ownership of projects and helping shape the engineering standards and technology that support GOSH Charity's future.

**Salary**

The salary for this role is £68,000per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office.

* Design, build, test and run secure, production-grade software across front-end, back-end and integration services.
* Take technical ownership of projects from discovery and architecture through to deployment and ongoing support.
* Design and build APIs, integrations and automations that connect our systems and external partners, including work within our Driven by Data transformation programme.
* Build and operate solutions in AWS, using modern DevOps and Infrastructure as Code practices.
* Contribute to our digital experiences, including our website and future web technologies, working with multidisciplinary teams to build solutions around user needs.

* Explore emerging technologies and approaches where they add genuine value, including automation, event-driven architecture and the responsible use of AI.
* Work with technical and non-technical stakeholders to understand the problem behind the request and develop solutions that deliver meaningful outcomes.

* Strong experience delivering complex, production-grade software from technical design through to deployment and support.
* Strong full-stack engineering experience, with the ability to architect solutions across both front-end and back-end technologies.

*Eugénie Humeau, Senior Insights Manager - EmergingTech*

Working alongside a team of researchers and specialists, you'll contribute to every stage of the research process, from evidence gathering and analysis through to stakeholder engagement, publication and dissemination.

We're looking for someone who is excited by the opportunity to work at the intersection of AI, digital innovation and international development. **Analysis** – Analysis is central to this role, enabling the interpretation of evidence, identification of trends and translation of complex information into clear, actionable insights that underpin high-quality research.

**Communication** – Essential for producing high-quality research outputs and communicating complex technical concepts clearly to audiences across industry, government and the development ecosystem.

# Mobile Automation Engineer

Solihull, England, United Kingdom

**OVERVIEW:**

We're looking for a Mobile Automation Engineer to join our Quality Engineering (QE) team, helping us build and scale automated testing for our iOS and Android apps. You'll add to and maintain the automation framework that catch issues before stakeholders ever see them, working closely with mobile developers, fellow automation engineers, and product teams to keep our releases fast and dependable.

This is a hands-on, mid-level role: you'll take ownership of automation suites and specific quality areas within mobile, while collaborating with senior engineers on framework direction and best practice.

**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:**

* Adding and maintaining automated tests for our iOS and Android apps in Java using Appium.
* Run and scale automated test execution across real devices and browsers using BrowserStack.
* Integrate mobile automation into CI/CD pipelines to support fast, reliable, and frequent releases.
* Collaborate with mobile developers and QE engineers to define test strategy and identify areas for automation coverage.
* Investigate test failures, distinguishing genuine defects from flaky tests, and drive fixes to improve suite reliability.
* Maintain and improve the Appium/Java test framework and our BrowserStack test infrastructure.
* Contribute to code reviews, share automation best practice, and help raise the overall quality bar across the mobile team.
* Report on test coverage and quality metrics to stakeholders across engineering and product.
* Explore and adopt AI and agentic tooling to speed up test creation, triage failures, and improve automation coverage.

**WHAT YOU'LL NEED:**

Essential Criteria:

* Experience in test automation, with meaningful hands-on experience automating native mobile applications (iOS and/or Android).
* Practical experience building and maintaining mobile automation frameworks with Appium.
* Solid programming skills in Java, object orientated programming.
* Experience with BDD frameworks (e.g. Cucumber).
* Experience running automated tests on BrowserStack (or a similar cloud device platform).
* Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (e.g. Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Bitrise, CircleCI).
* Understanding of mobile app architecture and the unique challenges of testing on real devices vs. emulators/simulators.
* A methodical, quality-first mindset with strong attention to detail and a knack for spotting edge cases.
* Good communication skills and comfort collaborating across engineering, QE, and product functions.

Preferred Skills:

* Experience with performance or accessibility testing on mobile.
* Familiarity with API testing tools (e.g. Postman, RestAssured).
* Exposure to other cloud device farms (e.g. Sauce Labs, AWS Device Farm, Firebase Test Lab).
* Experience working in an e-commerce or consumer app environment.
* Curiosity about, or hands-on experience with, AI-assisted or agentic testing tools.

## Job Introduction

 

Handelsbanken is a relationship bank built on trust, long-term thinking and local decision-making. We provide bespoke banking and wealth management services to personal and corporate customers,

Our decentralised model means decisions are made close to the customer, in our branches. Our central Functions teams play a vital role in supporting the branch network, providing the expertise, governance and infrastructure that enable branches to serve customers effectively and sustainably.

**The opportunity** 

Reporting to the Head of Wealth and forming part of the Wealth Management Leadership team, the Head of Professional Standards & Quality leads the development, implementation and oversight of professional standards, accreditation, quality assurance, business governance and MI across the Wealth business, so that our advice is consistently high-quality, compliant and delivered in the client’s best interest.

This is a senior, strategic leadership role, accountable for the quality of advice and the professional standards that sit behind it across the business. It sets direction, shapes standards and holds the functions within its remit to account.

The role leads the Standards & Quality function and owns the Training & Competency (T&C) scheme as it applies to advice, covering both Area Managers and Client Directors. A central function that underpins the advice process sits within its oversight remit.

The Wealth Assurance Team provides independent file review and quality assurance of advice, evidencing good client outcomes under Consumer Duty evidenced through provision of relevant MI.

This role can be based in either London, Tunbridge Wells or Manchester offices with the requirement for the successful candidate to travel to the other offices on occasion.

**Leadership & strategic oversight**

* Draw on management information and outcomes data to assure the quality of advice, evidence good client outcomes and drive continuous improvement.

**Professional standards, accreditation & quality of advice**

**Wealth Assurance Team**

**Governance, regulatory & stakeholder**

* Ensure effective governance, compliance and enforcement of professional standards, with sound record keeping and clear management information.
* Lead and embed a culture of integrity and compliance, building a client-first culture and acting in the client’s best interest, with oversight of regular training on regulatory change and good practice.

**i2 Group**, a **Harris Computer company**, is seeking a **Platform** **Software Engineer** on a full-time, permanent, remote basis with a monthly requirement of attending the i2 Group offices in Cambridge.

**The Role**  
The Platform team solves one of the harder problems in software delivery: getting the same product to work correctly on a developer's laptop, a cloud cluster, a multi-node on-premise deployment, and a fully air-gapped system. None of those environments are ones we control once deployed, and loose intent produces different results on each of them. The job is deciding precisely what has to be true everywhere, and then building it.  
Alongside customer-facing delivery, the team builds the internal platform capabilities that let our R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software. It is our second priority and the area where our AI-first workflows have moved fastest.  
We are a small team, working closely with Architects, UX Designers, and Product Managers. We are looking for engineers who can define, design, and build platform capabilities, rather than simply maintain them.

**How We Work**

We are AI-first. The bottleneck has shifted from writing to thinking, the AI writes the code, you own the decisions that shape it. If you have worked this way before, you'll recognise the workflow immediately. If you haven't, it's a shift in how you think about your time. Your focus is on the decisions, not the code that expresses them.Deep expertise in a specific tool stack matters less than it once did. What counts is knowing what good looks like — enough domain awareness to write a meaningful spec, ask the right questions, and develop an instinct for where AI helps, where it misleads, and when not to trust it.

Whether you come from an AI-first background or a platform engineering background, you are welcome here. The AI-first developer brings rigour and reasoning; the platform engineer brings domain knowledge and an instinct for what good looks like. Either way, we'll help you get there.

**What You'll Be Doing**

The precision described above is not a separate activity from delivery — it is how we deliver. In practice the role covers:

* Designing, building, and maintaining the software and tooling used to deploy, configure, and operate i2's products across desktop, single-box, on-premise, and cloud targets
* Building production-grade container images and the interfaces they expose to hosting platforms
* Owning the deployment and upgrade story for stateful distributed components, including recovery paths from shapes already shipped to customers
* Delivering releases to customers across diverse and often restricted environments, and supporting the upgrade paths from what is already in the field
* Developing internal platform capabilities that let R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software
* Maintaining and improving CI/CD pipelines and internal developer tooling
* Instrumenting deployments and the delivery pipeline so that decisions are made on data
* Contributing to architectural decisions, validating that what gets built matches what was specified, and owning the quality of AI-generated output
* Owning the testing strategy for deployments

**What We're Looking For**

The things we care most about are the ones that are hardest to teach: a spec-first way of working, design thinking, and the judgement to know when something that looks right is not.

Specifically:

* You can take a vague requirement, interrogate it, record the decision and its trade-offs, and define the test that would prove it wrong
* You can decompose a system into components with clear responsibilities, decide where a boundary belongs, and be concrete about what crosses it and how it is authenticated
* You are AI-first or ready to commit to it — not just willing to try it alongside your existing workflow
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code — you have built deployments on a major cloud and understand the tooling
* You have the judgement to recognise when AI output is wrong — a plausible implementation that quietly violates a security invariant, or a port that looks correct and is not
* You are comfortable working in technologies and deployment topologies you have not encountered before, and you learn them quickly

The technical depth we look for sits alongside those traits, not above them. We want experience in platform or software engineering in a commercial environment — enough exposure to deployment and operational concerns to write meaningful specs and validate AI output against them:

* Experience shipping software to structurally different deployment targets; you understand why they differ, not just that they do
* Container technology: you have built and shipped production-grade images, not just run them locally
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code: you have worked with AWS and understand the tooling
* Application security: you understand trust boundaries, identity models, and secrets handling
* CI/CD pipelines: you have built and maintained them, not just consumed them
* You can work effectively with engineers, architects, and non-technical stakeholders
* The role may require UK national Security Check (SC) vetting;

  candidates must be eligible for and willing to undergo this if needed.
* Bachelor's degree in software engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience

**What You'll Work With**

These are the technologies you will be working with day to day:

* AI coding tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) as the primary development workflow
* AWS today, with Azure and Google Cloud planned
* Infrastructure as code: AWS CDK and CloudFormation
* CI/CD with CircleCI and internal developer tooling
* Docker and production image pipelines
* Deployment tooling for Windows and Linux, including desktop installer and packaging
* Apache Solr, ZooKeeper, DB2, SQL Server, Postgres

i2 Group is the global leader in advanced visual analysis solutions. We empower analysts and investigators to discover, create, and disseminate actionable intelligence to combat threats including crime, terrorism, war, and fraud. Our software helps analysts transform data in real time, enabling customers to detect, disrupt, and defeat sophisticated threats across law enforcement, fraud and financial crime, military defence, and national security.

## **Why Hawk-Eye & Why Tennis?**

Join us at Hawk-Eye and be part of an exhilarating journey through the world of sports events. Our operations teams play a crucial role in delivering high-quality experiences at major sporting events worldwide. These are the different areas that you can explore:

* **Technical**: Testing, improving and stress testing our systems to enhance the performance of our delivery across the tours.
* **Creative**: Working closely with TV directors and external broadcasters to provide statistics and storytelling of insights across tennis matches during live broadcasts.
* **Operations**: Reviewing, improving and strategising how we improve the efficiency of delivery across the globe.
* **Projects:** On-site management of our service delivery across the globe. Liaising with external stakeholders to organise our technical requirements to be ready and sites to be prepared for our arrival, and to deliver our services to the deadline of the events.
* **Broadcast Production**: Rigging and directing live TV broadcasts across the Masters 1000s ATP tour.

**» Who is the Tennis Technical Team?**

The Tennis Technical Team oversees all technical aspects of the department, including the planning and delivery of our technology at events, testing and roll out of new software releases and new products, and advising on hardware specifications. They also directly impact the long term product roadmaps for tennis through reporting bugs, feature requests and new ideas through to the Product and Development teams.

As Data Lead you will fit in as part of the technical pillar within Tennis. At each event there is a Technical Guarantee whose role it is to oversee our full technical delivery including the delivery of our data - this includes the hardware and software set up of Hawk-Eye’s Tennis Data Platform on site. It is this data platform that you as Data Lead will oversee and manage from event to event, ensuring we are producing data that is not only accurate but also distributed in a timely fashion to all contracted clients, meeting all quality of service requirements and service level agreements.

As part of the technical team you will also be regularly interacting with the Product team in order to report detailed findings on the Tennis Data Platform and to continuously move the product forward, ensuring that it is as easy to use as possible. You will also liaise with the Commercial team and Clients to understand all delivery requirements, new services & products requiring data feeds, and advise on the contractual commitments of Hawk-Eye’s data delivery. Equally you will play a pivotal role in educating the operations team to ensure they are best set up for success at every event.

**» What the job is all about**

The role is all about managing the day to day data services that we deliver across all our Tennis events that take place around the globe. In 2021 we rolled out our Tennis Data Platform which manages and produces a whole host of data feeds that are then distributed at various latencies to clients and third parties, as well as used internally to drive products. The management of this live service is essential as well as the storage of the historical data for future use. Data capture and delivery is one of the key foundational services that we provide in the tennis market requiring technical expertise, high attention to detail and well organised individuals to manage it.

Alongside the day to day management of live delivery, the Data Lead will also be driving and testing improvements while working to bring new features to the Tennis Data Platform that improve various aspects of Hawk-Eye’s overall service delivery at tennis events around the World. Equally, the Data Lead will be responsible for onboarding new clients, and supporting the testing of new feeds and features with existing clients.

Our data performance is constantly being assessed by meeting necessary contract service levels. A big part of this role will be producing and assessing data delivery reports, to provide both clients and senior tennis stakeholders with an accurate picture of our data performance from event to event, pinpointing areas of improvement and then helping to implement changes both technically and operationally to address those identified problem areas.

**i2 Group**, a **Harris Computer company**, is seeking a **Platform** **Software Engineer** on a full-time, permanent, remote basis with a monthly requirement of attending the i2 Group offices in Cambridge.

**The Role**  
The Platform team solves one of the harder problems in software delivery: getting the same product to work correctly on a developer's laptop, a cloud cluster, a multi-node on-premise deployment, and a fully air-gapped system. None of those environments are ones we control once deployed, and loose intent produces different results on each of them. The job is deciding precisely what has to be true everywhere, and then building it.  
Alongside customer-facing delivery, the team builds the internal platform capabilities that let our R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software. It is our second priority and the area where our AI-first workflows have moved fastest.  
We are a small team, working closely with Architects, UX Designers, and Product Managers. We are looking for engineers who can define, design, and build platform capabilities, rather than simply maintain them.

**How We Work**

We are AI-first. The bottleneck has shifted from writing to thinking, the AI writes the code, you own the decisions that shape it. If you have worked this way before, you'll recognise the workflow immediately. If you haven't, it's a shift in how you think about your time. Your focus is on the decisions, not the code that expresses them.Deep expertise in a specific tool stack matters less than it once did. What counts is knowing what good looks like — enough domain awareness to write a meaningful spec, ask the right questions, and develop an instinct for where AI helps, where it misleads, and when not to trust it.

Whether you come from an AI-first background or a platform engineering background, you are welcome here. The AI-first developer brings rigour and reasoning; the platform engineer brings domain knowledge and an instinct for what good looks like. Either way, we'll help you get there.

**What You'll Be Doing**

The precision described above is not a separate activity from delivery — it is how we deliver. In practice the role covers:

* Designing, building, and maintaining the software and tooling used to deploy, configure, and operate i2's products across desktop, single-box, on-premise, and cloud targets
* Building production-grade container images and the interfaces they expose to hosting platforms
* Owning the deployment and upgrade story for stateful distributed components, including recovery paths from shapes already shipped to customers
* Delivering releases to customers across diverse and often restricted environments, and supporting the upgrade paths from what is already in the field
* Developing internal platform capabilities that let R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software
* Maintaining and improving CI/CD pipelines and internal developer tooling
* Instrumenting deployments and the delivery pipeline so that decisions are made on data
* Contributing to architectural decisions, validating that what gets built matches what was specified, and owning the quality of AI-generated output
* Owning the testing strategy for deployments

**What We're Looking For**

The things we care most about are the ones that are hardest to teach: a spec-first way of working, design thinking, and the judgement to know when something that looks right is not.

Specifically:

* You can take a vague requirement, interrogate it, record the decision and its trade-offs, and define the test that would prove it wrong
* You can decompose a system into components with clear responsibilities, decide where a boundary belongs, and be concrete about what crosses it and how it is authenticated
* You are AI-first or ready to commit to it — not just willing to try it alongside your existing workflow
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code — you have built deployments on a major cloud and understand the tooling
* You have the judgement to recognise when AI output is wrong — a plausible implementation that quietly violates a security invariant, or a port that looks correct and is not
* You are comfortable working in technologies and deployment topologies you have not encountered before, and you learn them quickly

The technical depth we look for sits alongside those traits, not above them. We want experience in platform or software engineering in a commercial environment — enough exposure to deployment and operational concerns to write meaningful specs and validate AI output against them:

* Experience shipping software to structurally different deployment targets; you understand why they differ, not just that they do
* Container technology: you have built and shipped production-grade images, not just run them locally
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code: you have worked with AWS and understand the tooling
* Application security: you understand trust boundaries, identity models, and secrets handling
* CI/CD pipelines: you have built and maintained them, not just consumed them
* You can work effectively with engineers, architects, and non-technical stakeholders

About IMU Biosciences
IMU Biosciences has developed proprietary platform technologies that generate and translate vast system-level immune data into actionable insights and tools to drive the development of precision medicines across a variety of diseases. Built on over a decade of research at King’s College London and the Francis Crick Institute, IMU leverages advanced immune profiling with proprietary AI and machine learning analytics to uncover novel clinical immune signatures. IMU continues to establish partnerships with leading pharma and biotech companies to advance disease diagnosis, optimise product selection, and improve patient stratification and monitoring - while also building its own pipeline of innovative products.
About the role
IMU is applying cutting-edge immune system science, data engineering, and machine learning to understand human health in a deeper and more actionable way. As our work moves closer to the clinic, we are building the data infrastructure needed to make complex biological and clinical data reliable, reproducible, governed, and ready for scientific discovery.
We are looking for a Software Engineer to help build and operate the platform behind that work. We think of the data platform as a product, not just infrastructure: it should be reliable, usable, well-documented, and shaped around the needs of the scientists, data scientists, and engineers who depend on it.
You will help turn high-dimensional biological data into trusted, reusable, analysis-ready data products, and you will build the infrastructure that allows teams to run reproducible pipelines at scale.
This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who lives in the cloud, expects infrastructure to be defined as code, and cares deeply about reproducibility. The work connects modern data platform engineering directly to cutting-edge science and, ultimately, better human health.
The role is hybrid, with an expectation of working from our London office a couple of days per week.
Team and ways of working
You will join a small, growing data platform function working closely with computational immunologists, data scientists, software engineers, and clinical-facing teams. This role sits in the platform layer: building the shared foundations that allow project teams to ingest, structure, govern, process, and reuse data reliably.
You will not be working in isolation, but you should be comfortable owning substantial pieces of the platform, making pragmatic technical decisions, and helping set engineering standards as the function scales.
What you will do
Build, maintain, and improve cloud-native data platform services used by scientific, data science, and engineering teams.
Develop and operate data lake and medallion-style architectures across raw, cleaned, curated, and analysis-ready data layers.
Create reliable patterns for data ingestion, validation, transformation, storage, metadata capture, and access control.
Support reproducible scientific and data pipelines, including assisting in the migration of workflows into production-ready deployable artefacts.
Improve data discoverability, lineage, provenance, auditability, and reuse in line with practical FAIR data principles.
Build automation, infrastructure, and developer workflows using infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, containers, and cloud-native engineering practices.
Work closely with scientists, software engineers, and platform users to turn real data problems into reliable platform capabilities.
Improve reliability, documentation, maintainability, and cost-awareness across data platform services and pipelines.
What we are looking for
Core experience
We do not expect every candidate to have used every tool in our stack. At CV stage, we are mainly looking for evidence of strong engineering judgement and hands-on experience in a few key areas:
Strong software engineering experience in Python or another production-grade language.
Practical experience building and operating cloud-native systems on AWS.
Experience with infrastructure-as-code, ideally Pulumi, Terraform, or an equivalent tool.
Experience with data lakes, medallion architectures, lakehouse patterns, or large-scale analytical data platforms.
Experience enabling, operating, or productionising data pipelines or scientific workflows.
Technologies we use or value highly
The closer your experience is to this stack, the faster you are likely to be productive, but we care more about depth and judgement than superficial exposure to every tool:
AWS
Pulumi, Terraform, or equivalent infrastructure-as-code
GitHub Actions or equivalent CI/CD
SQLMesh or equivalent SQL-based transformation, modelling, testing, and deployment framework
Containers and modern DevOps practices
Data lakes, object storage, metadata, validation, schema management, and data lifecycle patterns
FAIR data principles, lineage, provenance, and governance
Nice to have
Experience with Seqera Platform and Nextflow for reproducible scientific workflow execution.
Experience with Dagster or Snowflake.
Experience in scientific, bioinformatics, computational biology, immunology, clinical, healthcare, or other regulated data environments.
Experience with lakehouse technologies such as Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi, Databricks, Athena, Glue, Trino, Spark, or DuckDB.
Experience with regulated software, security, quality, or healthcare frameworks such as IEC 62304, ISO 27001, ISO 13485, HTA, HIPAA, or similar.
Experience building self-service data platforms, internal developer platforms, or platform capabilities for data science teams.
What success looks like
You will help make the data platform a dependable foundation for scientific discovery and decision-making. Success means data is easier to find, easier to trust, easier to reuse, and easier to process reproducibly.
Scientific and data teams should be able to spend less time fighting infrastructure, tracing data provenance, or manually moving data between systems, and more time generating insight.
Why join us
IMU is building a company around a big scientific idea: that a deeper, data-driven understanding of the immune system can change how we understand, monitor, and ultimately improve human health.
We work with rich, complex biological data and combine scientific expertise, machine learning, and modern data infrastructure to generate insight from the immune system. Our work is moving closer to the clinic, which means the platform we build now has to support both rapid discovery and the discipline needed for future clinical and regulated use.
This is a rare opportunity to join at the point where the foundations are still being shaped. You will not be maintaining a legacy estate or simply keeping dashboards alive. You will help define how data is structured, governed, processed, discovered, and reused across the organisation.
The team is collaborative, scientifically curious, and pragmatic. We value strong engineering, clear ownership, sensible architecture, and people who can work effectively across disciplines while staying focused on practical delivery and real scientific outcomes.
You will also have room to grow. The data platform is central to IMU's future, so this role offers the chance to influence technical direction, shape engineering standards, and build systems that can scale with the company as we move from discovery toward clinical impact.
We support hybrid working, with time in our London office a couple of days per week, and flexibility around how people do their best work.

* Lead the product strategy, design and launch of a partner-delivered Cash ISA.

**About Javelin**

Javelin Global Commodities is a leading global commodities marketing, trading, logistics services and investment firm with head offices in London and wider global offices in New York, Dallas, San Diego, St Louis, Canada, Switzerland, Poland, Dubai, India, Singapore, China and Australia. Javelin was founded in 2015 and now operates across six continents with respect to more than 20 different commodities across thermal coal, metallurgical coal, iron ore, steel scrap, metals, hydrocarbons, freight, agriculture, and renewables.

Established in 2015, Javelin employs over 200 people and is a unique place to grow your career. We take pride in our values, global reach, meritocratic culture and strong work ethic. Our success over the years has been built on our guiding principles of customer service, creativity, transparency, integrity, and responsibility.

Whilst our footprint grows, we still foster a small-company atmosphere. We have a flat company structure and encourage collaboration across all seniority levels, teams and locations to generate the best ideas. Javelin has a dedicated strategy to support local and meaningful charities through volunteer days, donation matching, a 'give as you earn' scheme and other fundraising activities. We are committed to the wellbeing of our colleagues and organise various social evenings, sports clubs and lunchtime activities. Our London office has on-site gym facilities and a golf/sports simulator. Discover more at .

**What to expect during your internship:**

Javelin's Internship offers a 6-week programme where our interns will rotate across the Operations department and get to experience what it is like to work at one of the world's leading commodity businesses.

**Induction weeks**

In your first 2 weeks you will be fully inducted into to the business. You will have small group sessions covering each department to give you full oversight of how the business runs, alongside team building sessions with your fellow interns to build camaraderie. You will be partnered with a mentor for the entirety of your time at Javelin. This will be an industry expert who will guide you and fast track your learning experience so you can maximise your time in the firm.

**Rotations**

Following your induction weeks, you will rotate between the various operations teams where you will gain more in-depth knowledge into how these teams work and how they contribute to the success of Javelin, specifically their key role in the lifecycle across all of our traded commodities. This portion of the program is a crucial time where our interns will get a feel for the career opportunities available at Javelin whilst working with industry leading professionals. At the start of the programme, you will be assigned a strategic project that you will develop and progress throughout your placement. Supported by your mentor, you will leverage everything you have learned across the business to create a tangible opportunity, improvement or new process that could deliver value to Javelin. During your final week, you will focus on refining and perfecting your project before presenting your recommendations and outcomes to the senior management team, including the CEO. This unique experience offers the chance to make a lasting impact while gaining an authentic insight into the fast-paced world of commodity trading.

* A strong interest in a career within the commodities industry
* Self-motivated and able collaborate effectively with a global team
* Time management and organisational skills with the ability to perform multiple tasks and prioritise work
* Excellent communication skills (listening, rapport building, negotiation)
* A creative mindset with a flair for problem solving

The interview process will comprise of 3 stages:

* Functional Interviews - You will then meet with members of each team you will be working with and asked competency-based questions to assess your ability

### 1. About processing of personal data

Personal data is all information that can be directly or indirectly linked to a living, physical person. Examples of personal data are: name, e-mail address, telephone number and IP address. Processing of personal data is any automated use of personal data - such as collecting, creating, analyzing, sharing, and deleting personal data.

There are laws and regulations on how companies may process personal data, so-called data protection laws. Different data protection laws apply to different types of use of personal data, and in different parts of the world. An example of a data protection law that is relevant for our use of your personal data, as described in this privacy policy, is the EU Data Protection Regulation (2016/679, "GDPR").

Most obligations under the GDPR apply to the so-called data controller. A data controller is the entity that decides for which purposes personal data will be processed, and how the processing will be executed. The data controller can use a so-called data processor. A data processor is an entity that is only allowed to process personal data as instructed by the data controller, and may not use the personal data for its own purposes.

We are the data controller when we process your personal data as described in this Privacy policy.

## Job Description

Posted Monday, 14 September 2026 at 17:00

Kids Planet is an independent, family run group of nurseries providing the highest standard of nursery care across the UK.

|  |  |

Kids Planet Day Nurseries is seeking an experienced Data Governance Lead to design, implement, and embed a robust data governance framework across the organisation. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this role is the dedicated owner of all matters relating to how data is classified, handled, retained, and protected throughout its lifecycle.

This is a newly defined role created to address identified gaps in data governance capability – distinct from IT Security, which is owned by the Head of IT. The Data Governance Lead will work collaboratively across nursery operations, People, finance, and digital teams to ensure every member of staff understands their responsibility for the data they handle, and that Kids Planet meets all obligations and sector-specific regulatory requirements.

The role will be central to evaluating, procuring, and operationalising specialised data governance tooling, including Data Loss Prevention (DLP) platforms, to give the organisation real-time visibility and control over its sensitive data estate.

Kids Planet Day Nurseries Central Support Office will be relocating to Altrincham in the coming months.

# Key Responsibilities

## Data Governance Framework

* Develop, own, and continuously improve the Kids Planet Data Governance Framework, including data classification schemes, data dictionaries, and data quality standards.
* Define and enforce policies covering data creation, storage, sharing, retention, archiving, and secure deletion across all business functions.
* Establish and chair a Data Governance Working Group, bringing together representatives from operations, People, finance, and IT to embed a culture of data stewardship.
* Maintain a comprehensive data asset register and ensure all critical data flows are mapped and documented.

## Data Protection & GDPR Compliance

* Act as the organisation’s subject matter expert for UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, providing guidance to all departments on compliant data handling.
* Manage and coordinate responses to Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs), erasure requests, and other data subject rights in line with statutory timescales.
* Conduct and maintain Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for new systems, processes, and third-party relationships.
* Maintain and test the organisation’s data breach response procedures, coordinating with the IT Security team and, where required, the ICO.
* Ensure Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) are kept accurate and up to date.

## Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Tooling

* Lead the evaluation, procurement, and implementation of the organisation’s DLP platform
* Define DLP policies and rules that reflect Kids Planet’s data classification framework, ensuring sensitive data – including children’s personal data – cannot leave the organisation inappropriately.
* Monitor DLP dashboards and reporting, investigating alerts, identifying patterns, and driving remediation actions.
* Oversee the AI data usage governance programme, ensuring that staff use of AI tools is controlled, audited, and compliant with the organisation’s acceptable use policy.
* Act as the business owner for all data governance tooling, managing vendor relationships and licence renewals.

## Third-Party & Supplier Data Governance

* Lead the data governance aspects of supplier onboarding, ensuring Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) are in place and proportionate data-sharing controls are enforced.
* Conduct periodic reviews of third-party data processors to confirm ongoing compliance with contractual and regulatory obligations.
* Maintain the organisation’s supplier data risk register and escalate material risks to the CTO.

## Training, Awareness & Culture

* Design and deliver data governance and data protection training programmes for all staff, tailored to role-specific responsibilities
* Produce clear, accessible data governance guidance materials and maintain a staff-facing knowledge base.
* Champion a ‘data-responsible’ culture across Kids Planet, ensuring data is treated as a strategic asset.

## Reporting & Assurance

* Produce regular governance reports for the CTO and Senior Management Team covering data quality metrics, compliance status, DLP incidents, and open risks.
* Support internal and external audit processes relating to data governance and data protection.
* Track and report on the closure of data governance-related audit findings and recommendations.

# Person Specification

## Essential

* Demonstrable experience in a data governance, data protection, or information management role, ideally within the education, childcare, social care, or regulated services sector.
* Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, and practical application of data subject rights processes.
* Proven experience designing and implementing data governance frameworks, policies, and data classification schemes.
* Experience managing DSARs, DPIAs, and Records of Processing Activities.
* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex governance requirements into plain-language guidance for non-specialist audiences.
* Highly organised with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously.

## Desirable

* Professional qualifications in data protection or information governance (e.g. BCS Certificate in Data Protection, CIPM, ISEB/IAPP, GDPR Practitioner).
* Practical experience evaluating or operating DLP, data discovery, or data classification platforms.
* Familiarity with AI data governance considerations and acceptable use frameworks for AI tools.
* Experience producing governance reporting for senior leadership or board-level audiences.
* Knowledge of the childcare regulatory environment (Ofsted, DfE safeguarding requirements) and how this intersects with data protection obligations.
* Knowledge of, or experience working within, recognised information security, privacy and quality management standards, particularly ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701 and ISO 9001, including supporting certification, surveillance audits and continuous improvement activities.

# What We Offer

* Salary of £50,000 per annum
* Contributory pension scheme
* 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
* Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
* Professional development budget and support for relevant qualifications
* Supportive, family-friendly working environment
* The opportunity to build a data governance function from the ground up in a growing, values-led organisation

We are unable to offer any kind of visa sponsorship for this role.

We embrace everyone. Our goal is to create a truly inclusive culture and diverse workforce. We break down barriers so you can be your authentic self and flourish!

We expect all staff and volunteers to uphold this commitment, and safeguarding training is a fundamental part of every role. All colleagues are required to complete regular training to ensure they understand and fulfil their responsibilities. A Disclosure and Barring Service Certificate is mandatory for all positions, and this role will be subject to enhanced checks as part of our safeguarding duties.

Figma and Adobe CC (After Effects, Premiere, Photoshop) as well as strong genAI skills
