# Associate Creative Director - Women's Lifestyle

LADbible Group is one of the world’s most engaged digital entertainment businesses, **reaching over a billion people globally and amassing more than 13.9 billion social views each month.** With a **powerhouse portfolio** across general lifestyle, entertainment, sport, gaming, and tech, our brands: - including LADbible, UNILAD, GAMINGbible, and UNILAD Tech, are some of the most recognised and culturally relevant on the internet.

LADbible’s Commercial Team, LAD360, is a powerhouse of creativity, strategy, and innovation - partnering with the world’s most iconic brands, from Google and Nike to Disney and Tesco. With a headcount of 150 and growing, LAD360 has rapidly become one of the most formidable forces in media, delivering culture-shaping campaigns. Our work has earned us top industry accolades, including **Commercial Team of the Year** at the 2025 Campaign UK Awards and **Media Brand of the Year** at the 2024 MediaWeek Awards. At the heart of it all is a relentless drive to push boundaries, tell bold stories, and connect brands to youth culture like no one else can.

**About the Role**

Our commercial team is looking for an **Associate Creative Director** who understands what makes young women laugh, gets them talking, and matters to them. With a focus on Betches UK, this is an opportunity to shape bold, funny, culturally relevant content that connects with a Gen Z audience.

We’re looking for someone with a passion for women’s issues and lifestyle, a sharp sense of humour, and the ability to turn audience insights into **standout, social-first branded content.** You’ll define what great looks like across both partnership campaigns and platform output, guiding the team from initial spark through to delivery.

You’ll lead creative ideation across short-form video, memes, reactive content and talent-led formats, creating work that feels native, entertaining and true to Betches UK’s voice. From dating and friendships to careers, pop culture and the issues shaping women’s lives, you’ll know how to find the relatable truth and turn it into something worth sharing.

This role sits at the heart of the team, leading and inspiring a multidisciplinary group of creative producers, editors, creators, and talent partners to deliver work that earns attention and drives real impact.

**What the opportunity looks like**

* Lead the creative development of women’s lifestyle branded content, with a focus on BETCHES UK, ensuring ideas feel native to the platform and true to the brand’s voice.
* Apply and evolve successful content formats into partnership work, while developing new formats that connect with young women.
* Oversee creative output across owned social channels, ensuring consistency, quality and platform relevance.
* Own the end-to-end creative output, maintaining a high standard across both always-on content and campaign moments.
* Shape and manage the idea pipeline, balancing reactive content with bigger, format-led executions.
* Champion humour and an authentic female perspective, finding fresh ways to reflect the experiences, interests and issues that matter to our audience.
* Lead, mentor and inspire the wider creative team, providing clear direction and elevating the quality of ideas and execution.
* Act as the senior creative voice in client conversations, turning briefs into strong, simple ideas and presenting them clearly and confidently.
* Collaborate cross-functionally to ensure ideas are both ambitious and deliverable within fast-paced production timelines.
* Stay tapped into Gen Z culture, platform trends and audience behaviour, ensuring all output feels current and relevant.

**Skills and experience we'd like you to have**

* Significant experience within a social-first creative, editorial or advertising environment, operating at a senior or leadership level.
* A proven track record of developing standout branded content that feels native to the platform, with a portfolio that demonstrates a strong instinct for humour.
* A passion for women’s issues and lifestyle, with an understanding of the different perspectives and experiences within a young female audience.
* Deep Gen Z cultural fluency, from creators and internet humour to the conversations shaping young women’s lives.
* Strong leadership skills, with experience guiding multidisciplinary teams and improving creative output.
* Experience working with established content formats and evolving them for different brands or audiences.
* Ability to think strategically while maintaining a strong grasp of execution, including comic timing, tone of voice and storytelling.
* Confidence working with and influencing senior stakeholders, both internally and client-side.
* Deep understanding of content performance and what drives engagement across key social platforms.
* Excellent writing and pitching skills, with the ability to shape and sell ideas clearly and convincingly.
* Comfortable balancing long-term creative direction with rapid, reactive content cycles.

**At LADbible Group we've rolled out blended working which means the majority of departments across the business (including London, Manchester and International offices) work in the office 4 days per week.**

**LADbible Group is an equal opportunities employer. We are determined to create a diverse group at all levels of our company and we welcome all members of the community to apply for openings with us. As the leading social youth publisher, we have a powerful global platform to better represent our audience and enable those that do not have equal opportunities to have their voices heard. As a business, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce, in an environment where everyone feels comfortable to be themselves.**

* **AI is the central-operating model:** not a tool or a future plan - but the way we run.

## **What You’ll Do**

As **Legl's Senior RevOps Manager**, you own how revenue moves through the business - from a lead landing in HubSpot, through signature, launch and ramp, to a customer using the product at the level we expected when they signed. Legl gets paid for what customers use, not how many we sign, so this role covers the whole funnel: Sales & Marketing, Launch & Implementation and Customer Success.

* **Own HubSpot as our commercial system of record - l**ead routing, pipeline stages, deal hygiene and the data model underneath them, so that the CRM reflects reality and sales leadership can forecast from it with confidence.

* **Track ramp and forecast usage -** follow every new customer from go-live against what we expected at signature, build a bottom-up usage and revenue forecast by account, and explain the gap between forecast and actual each month to CS, Sales and Finance.
* **Build the reporting leadership runs on -** maintain the core commercial reporting in HubSpot and Metabase, write your own SQL when the standard reports don't answer the question, and get usage and revenue data in front of AEs and CSMs inside the CRM.
* **Find where deals slow down and fix it -** analyse cycle time by stage and segment, take the findings to the sales team, and drive the changes that speed deals up.
* **Lead change across the commercial motion -** when the sales or CS playbook needs to change, design the new process, document it, land it with the team, and report back on what worked and what didn't.

# Legal Engineer - Applied AI Knowledge

## About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.  
  
Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.  
  
1,000+ customers across 50+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to **$100M+ in ARR**, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI and Graceview.  
  
We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.  
  
Joining Legora means three things.

* We **lean in:** ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.
* We **fight for excellence:** high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.
* We **grow together:** as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

**What you'll do**

Legal AI is inventing its best practices in real time, and this role sits where that happens. You'll sit within the Legal Engineering team and work hand in hand with Product at one of the fastest-growing legal AI companies in the world, seeing new capabilities before almost anyone else, experimenting with them against real legal work, and turning what you learn into the standards a global function runs on. In a year here, you will see and vet more legal AI use cases than most people in the industry see in a career, working directly with some of the best legal engineers in the industry.

This is a judgement role, not a filing one. You'll be the person who vets the skills, workflows and use cases the function ships: testing them hands-on, separating the genuinely strong from the merely plausible, and quality-controlling practice-area workflows so that what carries the Legora name is consistently excellent. You'll research and experiment with prompting techniques and applied AI methods, author the exemplar use cases the rest of the function copies, and teach what you learn: delivering technical onboarding for new Legal Engineers in your region and broadcasting best practices to the team worldwide. And because judgement needs grounding, around 30% of your time stays on live client work, chosen for what it teaches.

**Specifically, you will**

• Vet the Skills Library and Legal Engineering outputs against the quality bar: review skills, workflows and use cases hands-on before they go live, and quality-control practice-area workflows for consistency.

• Research and experiment with prompting techniques, skill patterns and emerging AI methods, and turn what works into best practices the whole function adopts.

• Author the reference use cases that show what great looks like, published as the exemplars others copy.

• Work closely with the Product team on up-and-coming capabilities: early hands-on testing, the first best practices for new features, and structured feedback from real use.

• Produce materials that would support the technical onboarding and training for new Legal Engineers in your region, such as best practices to create use cases etc.

• Communicate new best practices, exemplars and platform changes to the Legal Engineering team worldwide.

• Support the flagship demos our CEO and C-suite take on stage at the industry’s biggest events: use case preparation, fixtures and rehearsal support.

• Oversee the quality and currency of the use case and skills libraries, including coordination across regions

• Spend roughly 30% of your time on live client work, selected for what it feeds back into the standards and libraries.

**What you bring**

You're a lawyer with real practice experience who has become genuinely technical: maybe you did a coding bootcamp, maybe you taught yourself, but either way you're the person colleagues ask how something actually works. You live in AI tools, and it shows: you can tell a strong use case from a plausible-sounding weak one, you know why a prompt underperforms before you've finished reading it, and you hold both halves of the judgement this role needs: what makes a prompt run well, and what makes a legal output substantively right rather than merely fluent. When you vet, you vet properly: line by line against the source, with the discipline to put the AI down when the job calls for your own eyes.

**We're looking for**

• A qualified lawyer with solid practice experience at a leading firm or in-house team, or equivalent: enough substantive judgement to vet outputs across practice areas.

• Real technical prowess: comfortable with code or scripting (a bootcamp or self-taught background counts entirely), and fluent in the mechanics of how AI tools actually behave.

• A heavy, habitual user of AI, ideally legal AI, with sharp prompt and use case discernment: able to rank a strong prompt against a mediocre one, articulate exactly why, and improve it.

• Visible pride in the craft of prompting and use case design: someone who wants to be the reference point for what good looks like.

• Rigour in review: line-by-line verification against source, and the judgement to know exactly when not to use AI.

• Comfortable running high-throughput workstreams: you triage well, keep many threads moving, and build process where volume demands it.

• Experience building skills, workflows or automations in a legal AI platform is a strong plus.

• Good to have: an M&A or wider transactional background, or deal coordination experience.

**Where this role can go**

This role is built to grow with the field itself. Applied legal AI knowledge barely exists as a discipline yet, and nobody accumulates evidence faster than the person vetting and testing the entire output of a global function. Do this job well and you are positioned to become one of the industry’s recognised voices on what good looks like. Inside Legora, the role is designed to grow into owning applied AI knowledge globally: the standards, techniques and systems every region operates on. Growth is subject to performance and company need, but the direction is deliberate: master the material here first, then define the standard for the industry.

**Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

**i2 Group**, a **Harris Computer company**, is seeking a **Platform** **Software Engineer** on a full-time, permanent, remote basis with a monthly requirement of attending the i2 Group offices in Cambridge.

**The Role**  
The Platform team solves one of the harder problems in software delivery: getting the same product to work correctly on a developer's laptop, a cloud cluster, a multi-node on-premise deployment, and a fully air-gapped system. None of those environments are ones we control once deployed, and loose intent produces different results on each of them. The job is deciding precisely what has to be true everywhere, and then building it.  
Alongside customer-facing delivery, the team builds the internal platform capabilities that let our R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software. It is our second priority and the area where our AI-first workflows have moved fastest.  
We are a small team, working closely with Architects, UX Designers, and Product Managers. We are looking for engineers who can define, design, and build platform capabilities, rather than simply maintain them.

**How We Work**

We are AI-first. The bottleneck has shifted from writing to thinking, the AI writes the code, you own the decisions that shape it. If you have worked this way before, you'll recognise the workflow immediately. If you haven't, it's a shift in how you think about your time. Your focus is on the decisions, not the code that expresses them.Deep expertise in a specific tool stack matters less than it once did. What counts is knowing what good looks like — enough domain awareness to write a meaningful spec, ask the right questions, and develop an instinct for where AI helps, where it misleads, and when not to trust it.

Whether you come from an AI-first background or a platform engineering background, you are welcome here. The AI-first developer brings rigour and reasoning; the platform engineer brings domain knowledge and an instinct for what good looks like. Either way, we'll help you get there.

**What You'll Be Doing**

The precision described above is not a separate activity from delivery — it is how we deliver. In practice the role covers:

* Designing, building, and maintaining the software and tooling used to deploy, configure, and operate i2's products across desktop, single-box, on-premise, and cloud targets
* Building production-grade container images and the interfaces they expose to hosting platforms
* Owning the deployment and upgrade story for stateful distributed components, including recovery paths from shapes already shipped to customers
* Delivering releases to customers across diverse and often restricted environments, and supporting the upgrade paths from what is already in the field
* Developing internal platform capabilities that let R&D teams self-serve infrastructure and software
* Maintaining and improving CI/CD pipelines and internal developer tooling
* Instrumenting deployments and the delivery pipeline so that decisions are made on data
* Contributing to architectural decisions, validating that what gets built matches what was specified, and owning the quality of AI-generated output
* Owning the testing strategy for deployments

**What We're Looking For**

The things we care most about are the ones that are hardest to teach: a spec-first way of working, design thinking, and the judgement to know when something that looks right is not.

Specifically:

* You can take a vague requirement, interrogate it, record the decision and its trade-offs, and define the test that would prove it wrong
* You can decompose a system into components with clear responsibilities, decide where a boundary belongs, and be concrete about what crosses it and how it is authenticated
* You are AI-first or ready to commit to it — not just willing to try it alongside your existing workflow
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code — you have built deployments on a major cloud and understand the tooling
* You have the judgement to recognise when AI output is wrong — a plausible implementation that quietly violates a security invariant, or a port that looks correct and is not
* You are comfortable working in technologies and deployment topologies you have not encountered before, and you learn them quickly

The technical depth we look for sits alongside those traits, not above them. We want experience in platform or software engineering in a commercial environment — enough exposure to deployment and operational concerns to write meaningful specs and validate AI output against them:

* Experience shipping software to structurally different deployment targets; you understand why they differ, not just that they do
* Container technology: you have built and shipped production-grade images, not just run them locally
* Cloud deployment and Infrastructure-as-Code: you have worked with AWS and understand the tooling
* Application security: you understand trust boundaries, identity models, and secrets handling
* CI/CD pipelines: you have built and maintained them, not just consumed them
* You can work effectively with engineers, architects, and non-technical stakeholders
* The role may require UK national Security Check (SC) vetting;

  candidates must be eligible for and willing to undergo this if needed.
* Bachelor's degree in software engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience

**What You'll Work With**

These are the technologies you will be working with day to day:

* AI coding tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) as the primary development workflow
* AWS today, with Azure and Google Cloud planned
* Infrastructure as code: AWS CDK and CloudFormation

Company description  
  
Ember Crows is an independent game studio based in London.  
  
We founded the studio to create original, story-driven games with distinctive worlds, strong artistic direction and stories worth playing.  
  
We’re a small and ambitious team. We care deeply about what we’re creating, but we also want Ember Crows to be a place where talented people can communicate openly, challenge ideas and enjoy working together.  
  
Website: https://embercrows.com  
  
Game description  
  
We’re working on ‘Names Go Dark’, a dark, narrative-driven third-person action RPG for PC and consoles, built in Unreal Engine 5.  
  
The game is set on Proxima b, a tidally locked planet divided between eternal light and endless darkness, combining science-fiction technology with Slavic mythology and a grounded, atmospheric world.  
  
Great RPGs need great stories, but they also need systems that make the player feel part of that world.  
  
We’re looking for a Game Designer — Systems & Gameplay to work directly with the Game Director and help turn the existing creative vision of ‘Names Go Dark’ into a coherent, playable and production-ready game design.  
  
A major part of the role will be developing and systematising our Game Design Document, identifying what still needs to be solved and working with the development team to turn those systems into gameplay.  
  
Responsibilities  
  
- Working closely with the Game Director to develop and formalise the gameplay vision.  
  
- Consolidating existing concepts, mechanics and design material into a clear Game Design Document.  
  
- Maintaining and developing the GDD as the project evolves.  
  
- Identifying gaps, contradictions and systems that still need to be defined.  
  
- Designing and documenting the core gameplay loop.  
  
- Designing player mechanics, combat, abilities, resources, progression and interactions.  
  
- Defining how different gameplay systems interact with one another.  
  
- Creating clear system specifications, diagrams, flows, variables and implementation requirements.  
  
- Designing enemies, encounters and player-enemy interactions.  
  
- Working closely with the Unreal Engine Gameplay Developer during implementation.  
  
- Prototyping gameplay systems where appropriate.  
  
- Reviewing implemented mechanics against the intended design.  
  
- Organising and analysing playtests.  
  
- Iterating systems based on feedback and actual player behaviour.  
  
- Making sure gameplay, narrative, worldbuilding and progression work together as one experience.  
  
- Helping the team prioritise features and keep scope realistic.  
  
- Maintaining clear, practical documentation that other disciplines can actually use.  
  
Requirements  
  
- At least 3 years of professional experience in Game Design, Gameplay Design, Systems Design or a closely related role.  
  
- At least one commercially shipped game or equivalent substantial production credit.  
  
- Strong experience designing and owning interconnected gameplay systems.  
  
- Experience creating and maintaining practical GDDs and system documentation used by a development team.  
  
- Experience taking gameplay systems from concept through implementation, balancing, playtesting and iteration.  
  
- Strong understanding of gameplay loops, progression, player feedback, risk/reward and balancing.  
  
- Good understanding of third-person action gameplay.  
  
- Strong understanding of narrative-driven RPGs and the relationship between gameplay systems, progression, narrative and worldbuilding.  
  
- Ability to turn high-level creative concepts into clear rules, behaviours, variables and implementation requirements.  
  
- Ability to design systems that reinforce the tone, themes and internal logic of the game world.  
  
- Experience working directly with programmers during implementation.  
  
- Experience working with a modern game engine.  
  
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  
  
- Ability to identify gaps, contradictions and systemic issues within an existing game design.  
  
- Ability to work independently and take ownership of significant areas of the game's design.  
  
- Very good written and spoken English.  
  
- Portfolio, shipped project, design case study or other professional work demonstrating systems you personally designed.  
  
Experience working on AA/AAA productions, RPGs, third-person action games, action-adventure games or similarly complex systems-driven titles is strongly preferred.  
  
We’re looking for someone who wants to design the game, not simply make documents look organised.  
  
If you don’t tick every box but have strong relevant professional work, we’d still like to hear from you.  
  
Nice to have  
  
- Unreal Engine 5 and Blueprint experience.  
  
- Combat and ability design.  
  
- Systemic gameplay design.  
  
- Enemy and encounter design.  
  
- Progression and resource systems.  
  
- Exploration or level design.  
  
- Experience balancing interconnected systems.  
  
- Experience with realistic, cyberpunk, science-fiction or dark atmospheric games.  
  
- Experience developing original IP.  
  
- Strong interest in or knowledge of Central and Eastern European history, culture, mythology and folklore.  
  
- Familiarity with Slavic mythology and folklore.  
  
- Experience with games drawing from real-world history, mythology or regional cultures.  
  
Where from?  
  
The role can be fully remote, hybrid or based in London.  
  
We have access to our Battersea workspace for people who want to collaborate with the team in person.  
  
For remote work, we ask for reasonable overlap with UK working hours so that design and development can move quickly together.  
  
What we offer  
  
- A central role in shaping the gameplay of a new original IP.  
  
- Direct collaboration with the Game Director.  
  
- Real influence over mechanics, systems and the player experience.  
  
- The opportunity to help define the design foundations and GDD of ‘Names Go Dark’.  
  
- Close collaboration with gameplay development, narrative and the wider creative team.  
  
- Flexible remote, hybrid or London-based collaboration.  
  
- A professional but relaxed culture where good ideas matter more than hierarchy.  
  
- Option to participate in Ember Crows’ project-based profit-sharing programme.  
  
- The opportunity to grow with the project and studio.  
  
This is a freelance contract. Compensation, scope and expected commitment will be agreed individually based on the role, experience and availability.  
  
What happens after I apply?  
  
- If, based on your CV, portfolio and previous work, we feel you might be a good fit, we’ll ask you to complete a short design test.

- The test will be based on a self-contained fictional or isolated gameplay problem and will not ask you to design production content for ‘Names Go Dark’.

You will work across a broad spectrum of chemical innovation, which may include polymers and composite materials, ionic liquids, sustainable and green technologies, food chemistry, battery technology and energy storage.

The role offers much more than routine prosecution. Depending on your experience, you will have opportunities to draft strategically important patent applications, advise on international patent portfolios, contribute to EPO oppositions and appeals, and gain exposure to contentious matters, including High Court proceedings.

You will be encouraged to develop direct client relationships and take increasing ownership of matters as your experience grows, supported by partners and colleagues who are recognised experts in their fields.

Working as part of our Chemistry team, you will:

* Draft high-quality UK, European and international patent applications covering a diverse range of chemical technologies.

* Advise clients on patentability, infringement, validity, freedom to operate and broader IP strategy, with appropriate support and supervision.
* Contribute to EPO opposition and appeal proceedings and gain exposure to contentious patent matters.
* Work directly with inventors, scientists and in-house IP teams to understand complex technologies and identify commercially important intellectual property.
* Build trusted client relationships by providing clear, pragmatic and strategically focused advice.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues across the firm and contribute to business development through activities such as articles, seminars, conferences and client presentations.

You will have a strong scientific background and a genuine enthusiasm for chemistry, innovation and the commercial application of intellectual property.

You will enjoy getting to grips with complex scientific concepts and be able to translate them into clear and effective patent strategies. * Part-Qualified or Newly Qualified UK and/or European Patent Attorney.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex scientific and legal concepts clearly.

MintNeuro is an innovative startup at the intersection of neurotechnology and semiconductors. We are pioneering integrated circuit solutions for implantable medical devices targeting the management and treatment of neurological conditions.

**Role**

As a Senior Digital Design Engineer at MintNeuro, you will lead and take ownership of the front-end digital design and verification for our next-generation mixed-signal ASICs ("Big A, Little D"). In our implantable neural interfaces, the digital subsystem plays a vital role in orchestrating, controlling, and monitoring ultra-low-power analog frontends, stimulation engines, and telemetry.

We are seeking an engineer who excels at writing clean, synthesizable Verilog/SystemVerilog and developing robust verification environments. You will play a key hands-on role in taking digital architectures from concept and specification through RTL implementation, front-end verification, synthesis handoff, and lab bring-up in a collaborative, fast-paced R&D team.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

***A. Digital Architecture and RTL Development***

• Lead the architecture, specification, and implementation of digital control, telemetry/serial communication, and power sequencing for mixed-signal ASICs.

• Develop clean, maintainable, and synthesizable Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL with a strong focus on safe, ultra low-power operation.

• Collaborate closely with analog IC designers to define mixed-signal boundaries, control register maps, clock generation, and analog calibration/trim routines.

***B. Verification, Safety and Quality Assurance***

• Define verification strategies and build self-checking testbenches (SystemVerilog) at block and system level to ensure thorough functional coverage.

• Implement functional safety and fault-tolerant mechanisms (e.g. state machine protection, parity/CRC, watchdogs, reset monitoring) for safety-critical product reliability.

• Perform front-end RTL quality checks including linting, clock/reset-domain crossing (CDC/RDC) analysis, and static timing review.

• Support product risk-management activities (hazard analysis, FMEA/FMEDA) and participate in design reviews for high-reliability systems.

You will be responsible for embedding operational excellence, reducing service disruption, strengthening resilience, improving user experience and ensuring operational risks are proactively managed and escalated. * Embed and maintain enterprise-scale ITIL-aligned service management practices, ensuring clear ownership, accountability and governance.
* Drive operational performance across infrastructure, cloud platforms, applications, workplace technology and end-user services.
* Develop and maintain enterprise resilience and disaster recovery capabilities, ensuring plans are tested, effective and continuously improved.
* Establish clear operational risk tolerances and escalation frameworks, ensuring risks are surfaced and addressed appropriately.

* Foster a high-performing culture that promotes accountability, collaboration and continuous learning.

### 1. About processing of personal data

Personal data is all information that can be directly or indirectly linked to a living, physical person. Examples of personal data are: name, e-mail address, telephone number and IP address. Processing of personal data is any automated use of personal data - such as collecting, creating, analyzing, sharing, and deleting personal data.

There are laws and regulations on how companies may process personal data, so-called data protection laws. Different data protection laws apply to different types of use of personal data, and in different parts of the world. An example of a data protection law that is relevant for our use of your personal data, as described in this privacy policy, is the EU Data Protection Regulation (2016/679, "GDPR").

Most obligations under the GDPR apply to the so-called data controller. A data controller is the entity that decides for which purposes personal data will be processed, and how the processing will be executed. The data controller can use a so-called data processor. A data processor is an entity that is only allowed to process personal data as instructed by the data controller, and may not use the personal data for its own purposes.

We are the data controller when we process your personal data as described in this Privacy policy.

**About Us**

Nothing is clearer to us than the belief that every woman should include strength training in her life to enhance both physical and mental well-being. It's about building strong bodies and even stronger minds, asserting their right to take up space in the gym, and allowing the spotlight to shine bright on their progress.

To us, strength training represents a determined, goal-oriented mindset and an unwavering work ethic. We don't wait for success; we create it through hard work and determination. When faced with challenges, we don't back down; instead, we break through barriers, recognising that true progress lies on the other side.

These are the pillars that form the foundation of Oner Active. We consistently challenge ourselves to create innovative and impactful products, so that you can perform better. With our range of products and innovative approach, we provide a wide variety of colours to ensure that all skin tones genuinely radiate in Oner.

**Our Purpose and Mission**

We are on a mission to unite and empower women to be the strongest version of themselves through strength training. We want to inspire women to take centre stage in the gym by promoting strength training, which underpins all movement and sport, as a healthy foundation in life.

**About you:**

Oner's people infrastructure needs to scale with the business, but not by building a single, all-consuming People function. We're splitting the work in two: a Talent team who own the full talent lifecycle from recruitment through to career development, and a People team who own everything that makes Oner a genuinely great place to work once people are here - culture, performance, capability, compliance, and the systems that hold it all together.

As People Director, you'll build a People function that goes beyond admin and process, and becomes a real driver of a high-performance, strength-based culture across the UK and US. This is the “once someone's here” half of the people function - the person who makes sure Oner is a place worth staying, growing, and doing your best work.

**You'll be responsible for:**

**Culture & High Performance**

* Own the Oner Mindset as a lived, everyday reality, not a slide in onboarding, but something embedded in how people are managed, reviewed, and developed
* Build and champion a genuine high-performance culture: clear standards, real accountability, and real support to meet them
* Lead the shift from reactive HR to strategic People partnership with the business
* Grow and actively embed culture into the US as it scales. Oner should look and feel like Oner wherever someone sits, not a UK culture with a US satellite bolted on
* Own onboarding end-to-end - from signed contract through to a new starter's first weeks - making sure their first experience of Oner feels considered and consistent, not just a Talent handover memo
* Find the specific mechanisms (rituals, comms, manager behaviours, physical/visual cues) that carry culture across distance and time zones, not just policy documents

**Internal Communications**

* Own how Oner talks to itself: build and maintain a genuinely great internal communications rhythm, not just cascade-and-forget updates
* Make sure key messages - from leadership, from People, from the business - land consistently and land well across both markets and all levels
* Treat internal comms as a culture lever in its own right, not an afterthought bolted onto other work

**Performance & Capability**

* Own performance management end-to-end: reviews, PIPs, warnings, probation - consistent, fair, and legally sound across both markets
* Recruit the L&D Manager as a first-90-days priority, then direct them in building capability and leadership development for the people Oner already has (career development itself sits within the Talent team — this is about building the skills and leadership bench once someone's on a path)
* Coach and develop line managers so that day-to-day people management improves, not just formal process

**Employee Relations & Compliance**

* Own UK and US employment compliance, policy, and risk - the two markets have different rules, and this role is the person who knows both cold
* Manage employee relations casework and escalations, with the judgement to know what needs legal input and when
* Exercise good judgement on when to push back on legal risk versus when to find the pragmatic, commercially sensible path through it - not every risk is worth the caution a lawyer's instinct defaults to, and not every shortcut is worth the exposure
* Keep policies (leave, benefits, conduct, flexible working) current, consistent, and genuinely usable, not just defensible

**Reward & Benefits**

* Own the benefits offering across both markets, making sure it reflects a business now operating transatlantically rather than a UK-only legacy structure
* Make sure contracts and benefits carry the same spirit and generosity everywhere, even where legal requirements and local norms force differences in the letter of them — the experience of being an Oner employee shouldn't feel like a UK offer and a US offer, it should feel like one philosophy expressed twice
* Partner with Finance on pay structure, benchmarking, and reward consistency

**Operational Excellence**

* Reduce key-person dependency by building resilient, documented People operations
* Own the People systems and data that let the business (and this role) see what's actually happening - turnover, engagement, performance trends
* Work as a genuine partner to the Talent team so a candidate's experience - from first interview through year three - feels like one joined-up business, not two functions that don't talk

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop the People team, setting clear standards and holding the function to a genuinely high bar
* Foster a collaborative, inclusive environment that prioritises continuous learning and improvement within the team and the wider business

**You'll need to have:**

* Proven People leadership experience through a period of real growth, ideally UK-based with strong, direct US employment experience - not theoretical, but having actually run compliance, ER, and benefits across both markets
* Previous experience operating at Director level, owning a function rather than a slice of one
* Previous experience at a fast-growth, founder-led company - someone who already understands the pace, informality, and founder proximity that comes with that environment, rather than arriving from a large corporate and needing to unlearn it
* A track record of building high-performance, strength-based cultures, not just maintaining engagement scores

* A clear, collaborative operator who can define a clean line between the People and Talent team rather than compete over territory

The Global Valuation team at Pacific Life Re is responsible for the actuarial valuation of our diverse lines of business across multiple markets and legal entities. The team produces and validates actuarial results supporting financial reporting, business planning and capital management processes, working closely with stakeholders across Corporate Actuarial, Operations, Finance, R&D, and Pricing.

The team is at the centre of an exciting transformation journey, driven by Project Unify and continued investment in actuarial systems, data and processes. **The Role**

You will lead the Savings & Retirement ("S&R") and Consolidation sub-teams within Global Valuation, with responsibility for the execution of valuation processes supporting the S&R line of business and consolidated reporting activities. You will be accountable for the delivery of quarterly and ad hoc actuarial outputs, ensuring results are produced accurately, on time and in accordance with the required control framework.

Working closely with the New Business and Actuarial Analytics & Insights teams, you will act as a key valuation stakeholder for new business transactions, providing technical input on valuation requirements, operational readiness and model implementation considerations. You will support the onboarding of new business into valuation processes and provide specialist support for particularly complex or novel transactions where additional valuation expertise is required.

Alongside S&R responsibilities, you will oversee the Consolidation team, ensuring the production and validation of actuarial results supporting Economic Capital and Bermuda reporting processes.

As a member of the Global Valuation leadership team, you will contribute to the continued development of the team and help promote a positive and collaborative culture within the London office. ****Job Description****

**The Role**

Following extensive global expansion over several years and a drive to standardise common systems and platforms globally, PL Re is undertaking a major back-office transformation programme and has established a Divisional Data Team to develop and manage an enterprise-wide data solution, reporting services and to embed best practice data governance.

We are looking to appoint a DevOps Senior to contribute towards the DevOps function within the Divisional Data Team (DDT). DevOps is the highest-risk pillar of the data engineering operating model, owning CI/CD, database change management, environment control, release management and platform access. The role holder will be the single point of accountability for how change moves safely from an engineer’s branch into production.

The role reports to the AVP, Data Engineering, who is responsible for prioritizing, planning and driving forward the data engineering and transformation activities required. The role holder will build close working relationships with data engineering, testing, reporting, architecture and IT infrastructure teams across our operating geographies, and will be responsible for ensuring releases are controlled, auditable and repeatable.

**Core Responsibilities**

Azure DevOps platform ownership  
•    Own the Azure DevOps organisation and project configuration for the Divisional Data Team, including projects, teams, security groups, service connections, variable groups and secure files.  
•    Administer permissions and access models across repositories, pipelines, artefacts and libraries, ensuring segregation of duties between engineers, reviewers and approvers.  
•    Manage build agents (including self-hosted agent pools), agent capacity, scaling and patching.  
•    Use Azure Boards to plan, track and report DevOps work, and integrate work items with commits, pull requests and releases for traceability.  
•    Manage Azure Artifacts feeds, package versioning and retention policies.

Git branching strategy and standards

•    Define, document and enforce the branching strategy across all repositories (for example trunk-based or GitFlow-style dev/SIT/UAT/production branches), including naming conventions and promotion paths.  
•    Set and maintain branch policies: required reviewers, minimum approvals, linked work items, build validation, comment resolution and merge strategy (squash, rebase or merge commit).  
•    Own the pull request process — review quality standards, approval routing, and clear rules on who may approve changes to which repository.  
•    Define the release branching, tagging and versioning model, and the process for hotfixes and emergency fixes.  
•    Own merge conflict resolution guidance, rebase and cherry-pick standards, and rollback procedures.

Git repository management

•    Create, structure and maintain repositories; define repository standards, folder structures, README and documentation requirements.  
•    Manage repository security, path-based policies, protected branches, forks and cross-repository dependencies.  
•    Implement and maintain pre-commit and pre-merge quality gates, including linting, formatting and automated tests.  
•    Manage repository hygiene: history management, large file handling, retention, archiving and repository migration where required.  
•    Ensure no secrets or credentials are committed to source control, supported by scanning and remediation processes.

Deployment and CI/CD

•    Design, build and maintain CI/CD pipelines (YAML-based) for Snowflake SQL, dbt models, Streamlit applications, stored procedures and supporting scripts.  
•    Own database change management (DCM), including the transition to and operation of a state-based deployment approach across development, SIT, UAT and production.  
•    Maintain consistent, reproducible environments and infrastructure-as-code, including configuration management across environments.  
•    Implement automated testing, deployment gates, approvals and post-deployment validation within pipelines.  
•    Ensure reliable rollback and recovery mechanisms for failed deployments.

Release management

•    Own the end-to-end release calendar and release process for the data platform, coordinating with delivery, testing and business stakeholders.  
•    Chair or represent the team at change advisory and release approval forums; prepare and submit change records (including ECRs) with appropriate evidence.  
•    Manage release readiness: entry and exit criteria, environment lock-downs, dependency management and go/no-go decisions.  
•    Maintain a complete and auditable release trail linking requirements, code, approvals and deployments to satisfy internal control and audit requirements.  
•    Conduct post-implementation reviews and drive continuous improvement in deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore.

Security, access and compliance

•    Own role-based access control (RBAC) design and administration across Snowflake and Azure DevOps, including role hierarchy, secrets management and privileged access.  
•    Implement and maintain data masking and PII controls, with documented approvals for access to sensitive data.  
•    Manage certificate renewals, artefact repository configuration and remediation of security scanning findings (for example Snyk and SonarQube).  
•    Ensure IT controls and Business Control compliance requirements are embedded within the delivery and release process.

**Qualifications & Experience**

•    Deep, hands-on expertise with Azure DevOps — Repos, Pipelines (YAML), Boards, Artifacts, self-hosted agents and service connections.  
•    Expert-level Git: branching strategies, branch policies, pull request workflows, tagging and versioning, merge and rebase, cherry-picking and rollback.  
•    Strong track record of designing and running automated deployment pipelines into production in a controlled, audited environment.  
•    Demonstrable release management experience, including change control, release governance and stakeholder coordination.  
•    Experience of database change management tooling and state-based deployment approaches.  
•    Strong working knowledge of Snowflake administration, RBAC, masking policies and cost/performance optimisation.  
•    Experience with dbt and SQL in a modern cloud data warehouse environment.  
•    Experience with infrastructure-as-code, scripting (for example PowerShell, Bash or Python) and monitoring/alerting tooling.  
•    Understanding of networking, certificates and security scanning tooling is an advantage.  
•    Excellent verbal and written communication skills, enabling effective collaboration with technical and non-technical stakeholders.  
•    Knowledge of reinsurance or insurance industry concepts is a bonus.

**Technologies**

•    Azure DevOps (Repos, Pipelines, Boards, Artifacts)  
•    Git  
•    Snowflake  
•    dbt  
•    SQL  
•    Database change management (DCM) tooling  
•    Infrastructure-as-code and scripting  
•    SonarQube / Snyk or equivalent code and dependency scanning

•    Takes responsibility for the quality, completeness and accuracy of own work and that of the team under them.

# Risk Manager

UK - Remote

**About Ping Identity:**

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

As Risk Manager, you will lead the identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring, and reporting of information security and business risks across Ping Identity. You will help ensure that risk decisions are consistent, evidence-based, clearly communicated, and aligned with the company’s objectives, risk appetite, and customer trust commitments.

You will partner with stakeholders across Enterprise Security, Engineering, Product, Legal, Privacy, People Team, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance to maintain and continuously improve Ping Identity’s risk management practices and supporting governance. Your work will connect enterprise risk management with the Information Security Management System (ISMS), Business Continuity Management System (BCMS), AI Management System (AIMS), control environment, customer assurance capability, and audit readiness.

You will balance strong risk oversight with pragmatic execution, helping the organisation understand its most material risks, make informed trade-offs, and track risk treatment through to measurable resolution. You will also contribute to a scalable operating model through clear governance routines, useful metrics, effective stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement.

## What You’ll Do

***You will:***

* Run and continuously improve the information security risk management lifecycle, including risk identification, assessment, prioritisation, treatment, acceptance, monitoring, and reporting.
* Run enterprise, business-unit, project, technology, and third-party risk assessments, ensuring risks are evaluated consistently and documented with clear business context.
* Maintain risk registers, risk statements, treatment plans, action owners, due dates, and escalation paths, ensuring material risks remain visible and actively managed.
* Define and monitor risk appetite, tolerance indicators, key risk indicators, and management reporting that support timely decision-making by security and business leadership.
* Advise senior leaders and control owners on risk acceptance, mitigation options, compensating controls, residual risk, and escalation requirements.
* Partner with control owners and business stakeholders to improve control design, evidence quality, remediation effectiveness, and the connection between controls and material risks.
* Maintain and improve the ISMS, BCMS, and AIMS risk components, including policies, standards, procedures, risk methodologies, control mappings, and governance records.
* Coordinate risk-related inputs to internal and external audits, customer assurance activities, regulatory requests, and security questionnaires.
* Oversee third-party and supplier risk activities, including inherent risk assessments, due diligence, risk treatment, ongoing monitoring, issue management, and exception handling.
* Establish governance routines, workflows, playbooks, service levels, and escalation processes that improve risk visibility, consistency, and operational efficiency.

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. Join the team responsible for developing the tests, tools, automation, and infrastructure that help ensure the quality of the software toolchain used to build every PlayStation®5 game.
You’ll collaborate closely with the ToolChain development teams to design tests and testing systems for new features as they are developed. You’ll also help design and implement internal tools, automation, diagnostics, and workflows that improve confidence in the quality, reliability, and maintainability of the product.
This role sits within Quality Engineering. That means our work goes beyond running tests or finding bugs. We build software that helps teams understand risk, improve feedback loops, diagnose issues faster, and build quality into the development process as early as possible.
Our toolchain is based on a private fork of the open-source LLVM project, continuously updated through an automated merge system. Thanks to our advanced continuous testing, we have a strong track record of identifying and reporting new bugs in the open-source project very quickly.
This role offers a great opportunity to build a career in Software Engineering in Test and Quality Engineering, working on industry-leading development tools. You’ll receive mentorship from experts in the field and have opportunities for continuous learning.
What you’ll be doing
Collaborating with development teams to design and implement tests, tooling, and test systems for new ToolChain features, helping build quality into the development process from the start.
Designing and developing internal tools that improve test execution, diagnostics, reporting, workflow efficiency, or developer feedback.
Contributing to testing tools and frameworks, improving how we validate the ToolChain and how quickly teams can understand quality risks.
Maintaining and improving test jobs on our Jenkins CI system, ensuring reliable execution, useful feedback, and opportunities to improve test performance.
Writing Python-based automation and scripts to support testing, analysis, reporting, environment setup, diagnostics, or workflow improvements.
Analysing automated test results to identify failures, patterns, trends, and areas where our testing, tooling, or infrastructure could be improved.
Investigating issues across test, build, tooling, and execution environments, helping determine whether failures relate to product changes, test issues, infrastructure problems, or environmental factors.
Supporting improvements to testability and diagnostics, making it easier for teams to understand failures and act on quality signals.
Participating in code and documentation reviews, offering feedback to improve test coverage, code quality, maintainability, clarity, and overall development workflows.
Learning and applying Quality Engineering practices, including risk-based thinking, automation design, test effectiveness, tooling quality, and continuous improvement.

A BSc in a relevant technical or scientific field such as Computer Science, Engineering, or Mathematics, or equivalent practical experience demonstrating appropriate technical skills.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, with the ability to design, implement, debug, and maintain code used for testing, tooling, automation, or infrastructure.
Understanding of software testing techniques, whether gained through academic coursework, personal projects, internships, or professional experience.
Interest in Quality Engineering, including how testing, automation, tooling, diagnostics, and good engineering practices help teams deliver better software.
Ability to write and maintain unit and system tests for software applications, ensuring quality and reliability. Experience developing testing frameworks is a plus for more experienced candidates.
Proficiency in scripting languages, such as Python, to automate test cases, workflows, analysis, diagnostics, or reporting.
Ability to build practical tools or automation, from small scripts that remove repeated effort through to more structured internal tooling used by the team.
An analytical approach to problem-solving, with the ability to investigate failures, understand patterns, and ask good questions when the cause of an issue is unclear.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey technical information in writing and verbally to team members with varying levels of expertise.
Collaborative mindset, capable of building strong working relationships and working effectively across teams, regardless of experience level or reporting line.
A learning mindset, with enthusiasm for developing technical skills, testing knowledge, tooling capability, and quality engineering judgement over time.
Nice to have
Experience in triaging software bugs and collaborating with development teams. For more experienced candidates, experience handling complex or ambiguous bug reports is a plus.
Experience testing released software products, particularly developer tools, compilers, SDKs, or similar platforms. Experience with more complex testing environments is valued for experienced candidates.
Familiarity with advanced software testing techniques, such as coverage-directed fuzzing, property-based testing, static analysis, or using sanitizers. This knowledge can be acquired on the job, so candidates with a learning mindset are encouraged to apply.
Practical knowledge of a system-level language such as C++ and the ability to navigate, test, or contribute to large codebases, whether gained through coursework, projects, or professional experience.
Experience with CI/CD systems, especially Jenkins or similar platforms.
Experience developing internal engineering tools, test utilities, dashboards, reporting tools, workflow automation, or diagnostic helpers.
Experience improving test reliability, maintainability, or reporting, including reducing flaky tests, improving failure diagnostics, or making automated results easier to act upon.

# Deputy Head of Financial Crime

## Location

London

## Employment Type

Full time

## Location Type

Hybrid

## Department

Business Operations

OverviewApplication

## **About Pleo**

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

## **About the role**

We’re looking for a **Deputy Head of Financial Crime** to join our financial Crime Operations team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help safeguard the firm against financial crime risks, lead critical remediation initiatives, and drive control enhancements as part of our Financial Crime Operations team as we scale our business spend management platform. If you're excited about building robust, future-proofed compliance frameworks and leading high-performing operational teams and are passionate about financial crime prevention and regulatory excellence, then this is the opportunity for you!

## **Who you’ll be working with and reporting to**

You’ll report to the Associate Director of Financial Crime Operations and work closely with teams in Compliance, Risk, Legal, Operations, and Product. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to mitigating AML, CTF, Sanctions, ABC, and Fraud risks while supporting sustainable business growth. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across the wider organisation, external auditors, and regulatory bodies to ensure success.

## **What you’ll be doing**

As a Deputy Head of Financial Crime, you will:

* **Drive Compliance oversight and quality assurance:** Oversee day to day financial crime reports, disclosures, risk assessments sign-off, and regulatory outputs while monitoring metrics and KPIs to address emerging risks and operational bottlenecks.
* **Lead Complex Remediation & Projects** : Act as the primary lead for financial crime remediation programs, regulatory look-backs, control enhancements, and tech integrations from scoping through to execution and root-cause analysis.
* **Provide Strategic Leadership Coverage:** Deputise for the Associate Director of Financial Crime Operations during absences, representing the function at executive committees, board meetings, and in regulatory engagements.
* **Direct Team Leadership & Capability Building:** Directly lead, coach, and empower the FinCrime Operations team, driving resource planning, talent development, and a high-performing, accountable culture.
* **Foster Cross-Functional & Regulatory Relationships:** Work closely with internal Risk, Legal, and Business units, as well as external auditors and regulators, to embed effective financial crime controls across the business.

## **What you bring**

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

* **Deep Financial Crime Expertise:** Comprehensive knowledge of AML, CTF, Sanctions, ABC, and Fraud frameworks within a 1LOD environment.
* **Strategic & Operational Leadership:** Proven track record of direct team management, coaching, resource allocation, and providing trusted counsel to senior stakeholders and boards.
* **Remediation & Program Management:** Hands-on experience leading multi-workstream remediation projects, regulatory look-backs, and complex control improvements.
* **Regulatory Acumen:** Strong understanding of evolving regulatory landscapes and experience engaging directly with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* **Data-Driven Problem Solving:** Strong analytical mindset to identify root causes, track KPIs, and optimize operational processes.
* A background in Financial Services, Fintech, or regulated payment institutions with at least 8+ years in financial crime/compliance, including 3+ years in a formal leadership role.

## **Why is this role a good fit for you**

This role is a good fit for you if:

* You enjoy balancing high-level strategic influence with hands-on operational execution and team leadership.
* You thrive in dynamic environments where you can lead complex remediation projects and shape evolving compliance frameworks.
* You want high visibility, direct deputising experience, and ownership over key regulatory and board-level interactions.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

* You prefer a purely advisory role without direct team management or operational execution responsibilities.
* You are uncomfortable working in fast-paced environments with shifting priorities or managing regulatory ambiguity.
* You prefer maintaining existing processes rather than actively driving process optimization and control overhauls.

## **How you’ll develop in this role**

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

* Lead key control enhancement and remediation initiatives to drive impact in our overall risk mitigation and operational efficiency.
* Collaborate with Operations, Risk, and Tech teams to improve fin-crime detection systems and workflow processes.
* Grow your skills in executive stakeholder management and strategic governance, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale.

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in fintech risk governance

## **The location**

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

## **Show me the benefits!**

* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis
* We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

## **The interview process**

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. Hiring Manager Interview: A 45-minute deep dive with the Associate Director of Financial Crime Operations focusing on operational experience, leadership, and technical expertise.
3. Challenge and Panel interview: We will send you a take home assignment to present into a panel interview
4. Final Interview: A final conversation senior leadership

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for a similar role, we received a total a vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

* CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!
* Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

## **About your application**

* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

The ideal candidate will have a qualification in computer science or a related subject, with a teaching qualification or significant teaching experience. A strong background in using relevant andragogical principles to develop engaging, relevant learning experiences, and experience of supporting educators would also be an advantage.

This is an exciting time for the Foundation, as we develop our Training Hub – a new purpose-built, self-hosted platform for our online courses. You will work within a product team along with other internal stakeholders to create a high-quality product for both classroom teachers as well as mentors supporting young people in our network of Code Clubs.

We work hard to make sure that the Foundation is a place where everyone is supported to do the best work of their careers. We have a flexible and collaborative approach to all aspects of our work. If you're the right person for the job, we’ll make it work for you, and you can be confident that you’ll be joining an exceptional team of people who care about our mission and each other.

* Contribute to the development of the Foundation's teaching and learning strategy and approaches. Actively engage with research and best practice, and identify areas for improvement and innovation.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation, and with external subject matter experts and partners.
* Engage positively with the Foundation's systems for quality assurance, including in relation to agreed policies for inclusion and accessibility.
* Proactively utilise user feedback and data to drive improvement.
* Represent the Raspberry Pi Foundation to external audiences and stakeholders as required.
* Contribute to the Foundation's thought leadership through writing articles and blogs, public speaking, and contributing to research and evaluation.

**Experience and personal attributes**

We recognise that everyone has the potential for growth. We welcome applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they have some, but not necessarily all, of the experience and personal attributes listed here.

* A thorough understanding of computing, with a degree or equivalent qualification or experience in computer science or a related subject.
* A teaching qualification, or significant experience of leading adult learning or a related subject.
* Experience in designing and delivering asynchronous online and synchronous in-person professional development to educators, preferably globally.
* Experience in supporting computing educators, and an understanding of computing pedagogy and andragogy within formal education and informal learning.
* Strong communication skills, including a high level of written English.
* Comfortable with a broad range of technologies, including hardware and software platforms, and the ability and willingness to learn new technologies as required.

* Willingness to travel in the UK and potentially internationally.

**About us**

The Raspberry Pi Foundation is an independent charity with a global mission to enable all young people to realise their full potential through the power of computing and digital technologies.

We empower schools to teach computer science and AI literacy through free curricula, classroom resources, purpose built software tools, and professional development for teachers. We inspire young people to become tech creators through the world's largest networks of coding clubs. We undertake original research that informs our work and which we use to advance the field of computer science education more broadly.

All of our resources and learning experiences are available for anyone to use at no cost. We are particularly focused on creating opportunities for young people who experience educational disadvantage and those who come from backgrounds traditionally underrepresented in technology industries.

Over the past decade, we have supported hundreds of thousands of educators and tens of millions of students. We have teams in six countries (India, Ireland, Kenya, South Africa, the UK and US) and partnerships with mission-aligned non-profit organisations in over 60 countries.

### Infrastructure Coordinator

Infrastructure - London, Kensington and Chelsea

---

About

The Rolex SailGP Championship is the most exciting racing on water, where anything can happen in short, adrenaline-fueled battles between national teams at iconic stadium destinations worldwide. Top athletes fly in identical high-tech F50 catamarans faster than the wind, at speeds in excess of 100km/h (60mph). Founded in 2018, SailGP is one of the world’s fastest-growing sports and entertainment properties, now in its sixth season.

SailGP also races for a better future, championing a world powered by nature. Underpinning the organization’s purpose-driven agenda is a diversification of the league, with the goal of immediately progressing gender equity and inclusivity.

Role Overview

The Infrastructure Coordinator plays a vital dual role within the Infrastructure team. Combining core administrative support with junior project and programme coordination, this role ensures the department operates efficiently day-to-day while maintaining strong alignment with SailGP’s central planning frameworks.

This position is ideal for an organised, proactive administrator looking to step up and build a career in programme coordination. You will take full ownership of essential department admin - focusing heavily on procurement support and team travel - while maintaining the operational "drumbeat" of the team. Working closely with the Infrastructure Director, you will manage weekly meeting agendas, track deliverables on Monday.com, and ensure the team hits its key One Event Plan (OEP) milestones.

Key Responsibilities

Core Department Administration & Logistics

* Procurement Support: Manage purchase orders (POs), invoice tracking, supplier onboarding, and procurement administration in close coordination with central finance and procurement teams.
* Team Travel & Onsite Logistics: Coordinate team travel schedules, accommodation bookings, and visa applications alongside the central travel team to support global event deployments.
* General Administrative Support: Maintain department document repositories, manage supplier contact lists, and provide broad administrative support to keep the Infrastructure function running smoothly.

Programme Coordination & Planning Alignment

* Team Cadence & Drumbeat: Maintain the operational drumbeat for the Infrastructure team, driving tracking on Monday.com to ensure deliverables and milestone deadlines are consistently met.
* Meeting Ownership & Reporting: Own the weekly team meeting agenda alongside the Infrastructure Director, utilising live One Event Plan (OEP) dashboards to review progress, track actions, and highlight upcoming milestones.
* Planning Framework Integration: Support the team in adopting standard planning templates, guidance, and governance processes, acting as the primary liaison with the Central Planning Office.
* Documentation & Dashboard Support: Help prepare operational planning documents, presentations, and status updates for internal reviews and senior leadership reporting.
* Continuous Improvement: Identify practical administrative or process improvements within the department and take ownership of assigned coordination tasks to drive them to completion.

Key Expectations

* Strong Administrative Foundation: Solid experience managing core administrative tasks, specifically purchase orders, invoice tracking, and travel coordination.
* Proactive & Organised: Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities, keep a team on track, and follow up on outstanding actions.
* Tech-Savvy & Systems-Focused: Comfortable working with modern project management and administrative tools (proficiency in Monday.com, Google Workspace, and procurement/ERP software is highly advantageous).
* Clear Communication Skills: Confident interpersonal skills with the ability to build strong working relationships within the Infrastructure team, cross-departmental administrative peers, and external suppliers.
* Growth Mindset: High level of initiative, attention to detail, and a genuine desire to develop project and programme coordination skills in a fast-paced, global sports environment.

Location 

Based in the UK with a requirement of at least 3 days per week in the London office.
